links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “OOP Basic Concepts”.

mcqs.question: Which was the first purely object oriented programming language developed?
mcqs.explanation: SmallTalk was the first programming language developed which was purely object oriented. It was developed by Alan Kay. OOP concept came into the picture in 1970’s.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a class?
mcqs.explanation: A class is Blueprint of an object which describes/ shows all the functions and data that are provided by an object of a specific class. It can’t be called as parent or instance of an object. Class in general describes all the properties of an object.

mcqs.question: Who invented OOP?
mcqs.explanation: Alan Kay invented OOP, Andrea Ferro was a part of SmallTalk Development. Dennis invented C++ and Adele Goldberg was in team to develop SmallTalk but Alan actually had got rewarded for OOP.

mcqs.question: What is the additional feature in classes that was not in structures?
mcqs.explanation: Member functions are allowed inside a class but were not present in structure concept.  Data members, static data and public access specifiers were present in structures too.

mcqs.question: Which is not feature of OOP in general definitions?
mcqs.explanation: Duplicate/Redundant data is dependent on programmer and hence can’t be guaranteed by OOP. Code reusability is done using inheritance. Modularity is supported by using different code files and classes. Codes are more efficient because of features of OOP.

mcqs.question: Pure OOP can be implemented without using class in a program. (True or False)
mcqs.explanation: It’s false because for a program to be pure OO, everything must be written inside classes. If this rule is violated, the program can’t be labelled as purely OO.

mcqs.question: Which Feature of OOP illustrated the code reusability?
mcqs.explanation: Using inheritance we can reuse the code already written and also can avoid creation of many new functions or variables, as that can be done one time and be reused, using classes.

mcqs.question: Which language does not support all 4 types of inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: Java doesn’t support all 4 types of inheritance. It doesn’t support multiple inheritance. But the multiple inheritance can be implemented using interfaces in Java.

mcqs.question: How many classes can be defined in a single program?

options.d: d) As many as you want

mcqs.answer: d) As many as you want
mcqs.explanation: Any number of classes can be defined inside a program, provided that their names are different. In java, if public class is present then it must have the same name as that of file.

mcqs.question: When OOP concept did first came into picture?
mcqs.explanation: OOP first came into picture in 1970’s by Alan and his team. Later it was used by some programming languages and got implemented successfully, SmallTalk was first language to use pure OOP and followed all rules strictly.

mcqs.question: Why Java is Partially OOP language?

options.a: a) It supports usual declaration of primitive data types
options.b: b) It doesn’t support all types of inheritance
options.c: c) It allows code to be written outside classes
options.d: d) It does not support pointers

mcqs.answer: a) It supports usual declaration of primitive data types
mcqs.explanation: As Java supports usual declaration of data variables, it is partial implementation of OOP. Because according to rules of OOP, object constructors must be used, even for declaration of variables.

mcqs.question: Which concept of OOP is false for C++?

options.a: a) Code can be written without using classes
options.b: b) Code must contain at least one class
options.c: c) A class must have member functions
options.d: d) At least one object should be declared in code

mcqs.answer: b) Code must contain at least one class
mcqs.explanation: In C++, it’s not necessary to use classes, and hence codes can be written without using OOP concept. Classes may or may not contain member functions, so it’s not a necessary condition in C++. And, an object can only be declared in a code if its class is defined/included via header file.

mcqs.question: Which header file is required in C++ to use OOP?

options.d: d) OOP can be used without using any header file

mcqs.answer: d) OOP can be used without using any header file
mcqs.explanation: We need not include any specific header file to use OOP concept in C++, only specific functions used in code need their respective header files to be included or classes should be defined if needed.

mcqs.question: Which of the two features match each other?
mcqs.explanation: Encapsulation and Abstraction are similar features. Encapsulation is actually binding all the properties in a single class or we can say hiding all the features of object inside a class. And Abstraction is hiding unwanted data (for user) and showing only the data required by the user of program.

mcqs.question: Which feature allows open recursion, among the following?

options.c: c) Use of pass by value

mcqs.explanation: Use of this pointer allows an object to call data and methods of itself whenever needed. This helps us call the members of an object recursively, and differentiate the variables of different scopes.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Classes”.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not type of class?
mcqs.explanation: Only 9 types of classes are provided in general, namely, abstract, final, mutable, wrapper, anonymous, input-output, string, system, network. We may further divide the classes into parent class and subclass if inheritance is used.

mcqs.question: Class is pass by _______

options.c: c) Value or Reference, depending on program

mcqs.explanation: Classes are pass by reference, and the structures are pass by copy. It doesn’t depend on the program.

mcqs.question: What is default access specifier for data members or member functions declared within a class without any specifier, in C++?
mcqs.explanation: The data members and member functions are Private by default in C++ classes, if none of the access specifier is used. It is actually made to increase the privacy of data.

mcqs.question:
Which is most appropriate comment on following class definition? 
class Student 
{
    int a; 
    public : float a; 
};

options.a: a) Error : same variable name can’t be used twice
options.b: b) Error : Public must come first
options.c: c) Error : data types are different for same variable

mcqs.answer: a) Error : same variable name can’t be used twice
mcqs.explanation: Same variable can’t be defined twice in same scope. Even if the data types are different, variable name must be different. There is no rule like Public member should come first or last.

mcqs.question: Which is known as a generic class?
mcqs.explanation: Template classes are known to be generic classes because those can be used for any data type value and the same class can be used for all the variables of different data types.

mcqs.question: Size of a class is _____________

options.a: a) Sum of the size of all the variables declared inside the class
options.b: b) Sum of the size of all the variables along with inherited variables in the class
options.c: c) Size of the largest size of variable
options.d: d) Classes doesn’t have any size

mcqs.answer: d) Classes doesn’t have any size
mcqs.explanation: Classes doesn’t have any size, actually the size of object of the class can be defined. That is done only when an object is created and its constructor is called.

mcqs.question: Which class can have member functions without their implementation?
mcqs.explanation: Abstract classes can have member functions with no implementation, where the inheriting subclasses must implement those functions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following describes a friend class?

options.a: a) Friend class can access all the private members of the class, of which it is a friend
options.b: b) Friend class can only access protected members of the class, of which it is a friend
options.c: c) Friend class don’t have any implementation
options.d: d) Friend class can’t access any data member of another class but can use it’s methods

mcqs.answer: a) Friend class can access all the private members of the class, of which it is a friend
mcqs.explanation: A friend class can access all the private members of another class, of which it is a friend. It is a special class provided to use when you need to reuse the data of a class but don’t want that class to have those special functions.

mcqs.question: What is the scope of a class nested inside another class?

options.d: d) Depends on access specifier and inheritance used

mcqs.answer: d) Depends on access specifier and inheritance used
mcqs.explanation: It depends on the access specifier and the type of inheritance used with the class, because if the class is inherited then the nested class can be used by subclass too, provided it’s not of private type.

mcqs.question: Class with main() function can be inherited.
mcqs.explanation: The class containing main function can be inherited and hence the program can be executed using the derived class names also in java.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is false, for a member function of a class?

options.a: a) All member functions must be defined
options.b: b) Member functions can be defined inside or outside the class body
options.c: c) Member functions need not be declared inside the class definition
options.d: d) Member functions can be made friend to another class using the friend keyword

mcqs.answer: c) Member functions need not be declared inside the class definition
mcqs.explanation: Member functions must be declared inside class body, though the definition can be given outside the class body. There is no way to declare the member functions outside the class.

mcqs.question: Which syntax for class definition is wrong?

options.c: c) class student{ public: student(int a){ } };

mcqs.explanation: Keyword class should come first. Class name should come after keyword class. Parameterized constructor definition depends on programmer so it can be left empty also.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs are similar?
mcqs.explanation: Class and structure are similar to each other. Only major difference is that a structure doesn’t have member functions whereas the class can have both data members and member functions.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is false for class features?

options.a: a) Classes may/may not have both data members and member functions
options.b: b) Class definition must be ended with a colon
options.c: c) Class can have only member functions with no data members
options.d: d) Class is similar to union and structures

mcqs.answer: b) Class definition must be ended with a colon
mcqs.explanation: Class definition must end with a semicolon, not colon. Class can have only member functions in its body with no data members.

mcqs.question: Instance of which type of class can’t be created?
mcqs.explanation: Instance of abstract class can’t be created as it will not have any constructor of its own, hence while creating an instance of class, it can’t initialize the object members. Actually the class inheriting the abstract class can have its instance because it will have implementation of all members.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Objects”.

mcqs.question: Which definition best describes an object?
mcqs.explanation: An object is instance of its class. It can be declared in the same way that a variable is declared, only thing is you have to use class name as the data type.

mcqs.question: How many objects can be declared of a specific class in a single program?

options.d: d) As many as you want

mcqs.answer: d) As many as you want
mcqs.explanation: You can create as many objects of a specific class as you want, provided enough memory is available.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is false?

options.a: a) Object must be created before using members of a class
options.b: b) Memory for an object is allocated only after its constructor is called
options.c: c) Objects can’t be passed by reference
options.d: d) Objects size depends on its class data members

mcqs.answer: c) Objects can’t be passed by reference
mcqs.explanation: Objects can be passed by reference. Objects can be passed by value also. If the object of a class is not created, we can’t use members of that class.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is incorrect?
mcqs.explanation: The array must be specified with a size. You can’t declare object array, or any other linear array without specifying its size. It’s a mandatory field.

mcqs.question: The object can’t be __________
mcqs.explanation: Object can’t be passed as function as it is an instance of some class, it’s not a function. Object can be passed by reference, value or copy. There is no term defined as pass as function for objects.

mcqs.question:
What is size of the object of following class (64 bit system)? 
class student {  int rollno;  char  name[20];  static int studentno;  };
mcqs.explanation: The size of any object of student class will be of size 4+20=24, because static members are not really considered as property of a single object. So static variables size will not be added.

mcqs.question: Functions can’t return objects.
mcqs.explanation: Functions can always return an object if the return type is same as that of object being returned. Care has to be taken while writing the prototype of the function.

mcqs.question: How members of an object are accessed?
mcqs.explanation: Using dot operator after the name of object we can access its members. It is not necessary to use the pointers. We can’t use the names directly because it may be used outside the class.

mcqs.question: If a local class is defined in a function, which of the following is true for an object of that class?

options.a: a) Object is accessible outside the function
options.b: b) Object can be declared inside any other function
options.c: c) Object can be used to call other class members
options.d: d) Object can be used/accessed/declared locally in that function

mcqs.answer: d) Object can be used/accessed/declared locally in that function
mcqs.explanation: For an object which belongs to a local class, it is mandatory to declare and use the object within the function because the class is accessible locally within the class only.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is wrong?

options.b: b) abstract class student{  }; student s;
options.d: d) abstract class student{  }; class toppers: public student{  }; topper t;

mcqs.answer: b) abstract class student{  }; student s;
mcqs.explanation: We can never create instance of an abstract class. Abstract classes doesn’t have constructors and hence when an instance is created there is no facility to initialize its members. Option d is correct because topper class is inheriting the base abstract class student, and hence topper class object can be created easily.

mcqs.question: Object declared in main() function _____________

options.a: a) Can be used by any other function
options.b: b) Can be used by main() function of any other program
options.c: c) Can’t be used by any other function
options.d: d) Can be accessed using scope resolution operator

mcqs.answer: c) Can’t be used by any other function
mcqs.explanation: The object declared in main() have local scope inside main() function only. It can’t be used outside main() function. Scope resolution operator is used to access globally declared variables/objects.

mcqs.question: When an object is returned___________

options.a: a) A temporary object is created to return the value
options.b: b) The same object used in function is used to return the value
options.c: c) The Object can be returned without creation of temporary object
options.d: d) Object are returned implicitly, we can’t say how it happens inside program

mcqs.answer: a) A temporary object is created to return the value
mcqs.explanation: A temporary object is created to return the value. It is created because the object used in function is destroyed as soon as the function is returned. The temporary variable returns the value and then gets destroyed.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct?

options.b: b) class student{  }s1; class topper{  }t1; s1=t1;
options.d: d) class student{  }s1; class topper{  }t1; s1.student()=s2.topper();

mcqs.explanation: Only if the objects are of same class then their data can be copied from to another using assignment operator. This actually comes under operator overloading. Class constructors can’t be assigned any explicit value as in option class student{  }s1; class topper{  }t1; s1=t1; and class student{  }s1; class topper{  }t1; s1.student()=s2.topper();.

mcqs.question:
Which among following is correct for initializing the class below? 
class student{
int marks;
int cgpa;
public: student(int i, int  j){
marks=I;
cgpa=j
}
};
mcqs.explanation: It is the way we can initialize the data members for an object array using parameterized constructor. We can do this to pass our own intended values to initialize the object array data.

mcqs.question: Object can’t be used with pointers because they belong to user defined class, and compiler can’t decide the type of data may be used inside the class.
mcqs.explanation: The explanation given is wrong because object can always be used with pointers like with any other variables. Compiler doesn’t have to know the structure of the class to use a pointer because the pointers only points to a memory address/stores that address.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “OOP Features”.

mcqs.question: Which feature of OOP indicates code reusability?
mcqs.explanation: Inheritance indicates the code reusability. Encapsulation and abstraction are meant to hide/group data into one element. Polymorphism is to indicate different tasks performed by a single entity.

mcqs.question: If a function can perform more than 1 type of tasks, where the function name remains same, which feature of OOP is used here?
mcqs.explanation: For the feature given above, the OOP feature used is Polymorphism. Example of polymorphism in real life is a kid, who can be a student, a son, a brother depending on where he is.

mcqs.question: If different properties and functions of a real world entity is grouped or embedded into a single element, what is it called in OOP language?
mcqs.explanation: It is Encapsulation, which groups different properties and functions of a real world entity into single element. Abstraction, on other hand, is hiding of functional or exact working of codes and showing only the things which are required by the user.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a feature of pure OOP?

options.c: c) Data may/may not be declared using object

mcqs.answer: c) Data may/may not be declared using object
mcqs.explanation: Data must be declared using objects. Object usage is mandatory because it in turn calls its constructors, which in turn must have a class defined. If object is not used, it is a violation of pure OOP concept.

mcqs.question: Which among the following doesn’t come under OOP concept?
mcqs.explanation: Platform independence is not feature of OOP. C++ supports OOP but it’s not a platform independent language. Platform independence depends on programming language.

mcqs.question:
Which feature of OOP is indicated by the following code? 
class student{  int marks;  };
class topper:public student{  int age;  topper(int age){ this.age=age; } };
mcqs.explanation: Encapsulation is indicated by use of classes. Inheritance is shown by inheriting the student class into topper class. Polymorphism is not shown here because we have defined the constructor in the topper class but that doesn’t mean that default constructor is overloaded.

mcqs.question: Which feature may be violated if we don’t use classes in a program?

options.b: b) Object must be used is violated
options.d: d) Basically all the features of OOP gets violated

mcqs.answer: d) Basically all the features of OOP gets violated
mcqs.explanation: All the features are violated because Inheritance and Encapsulation won’t be implemented. Polymorphism and Abstraction are still possible in some cases, but the main features like data binding, object use and etc won’t be used hence the use of class is must for OOP concept.

mcqs.question: How many basic features of OOP are required for a programming language to be purely OOP?
mcqs.explanation: There are 7 basic features that define whether a programing language is pure OOP or not. The 4 basic features are inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation and abstraction. Further, one is, object use is must, secondly, message passing and lastly, Dynamic binding.

mcqs.question: The feature by which one object can interact with another object is _____________
mcqs.explanation: The interaction between two object is called the message passing feature. Data transfer is not a feature of OOP. Also, message reading is not a feature of OOP.

mcqs.question: ___________ underlines the feature of Polymorphism in a class.
mcqs.explanation: Virtual Functions can be defined in any class using the keyword virtual. All the classes which inherit the class containing the virtual function, define the virtual function as required. Redefining the function on all the derived classes according to class and use represents polymorphism.

mcqs.question: Which feature in OOP is used to allocate additional function to a predefined operator in any language?
mcqs.explanation: The feature is operator overloading. There is not a feature named operator overriding specifically. Function overloading and overriding doesn’t give addition function to any operator.

mcqs.question: Which among doesn’t illustrates polymorphism?
mcqs.explanation: Function overriding doesn’t illustrate polymorphism because the functions are actually different and theirs scopes are different. Function and operator overloading illustrate proper polymorphism. Virtual functions show polymorphism because all the classes which inherit virtual function, define the same function in different ways.

mcqs.question: Exception handling is a feature of OOP.
mcqs.explanation: Exception handling is a feature of OOP as it includes classes concept in most of the cases. Also it may come handy while using inheritance.

mcqs.question: Which among the following, for a pure OOP language, is true?

options.a: a) The language should follow 3 or more features of OOP
options.b: b) The language should follow at least 1 feature of OOP
options.c: c) The language must follow only 3 features of OOP
options.d: d) The language must follow all the rules of OOP

mcqs.answer: d) The language must follow all the rules of OOP
mcqs.explanation: The language must follow all the rules of OOP to be called a purely OOP language. Even if a single OOP feature is not followed, then it’s known to be a partially OOP language.

mcqs.question: Does OOP provide better security than POP?

options.a: a) Always true for any programming language
options.b: b) May not be true with respect to all programming languages
options.c: c) It depends on type of program

mcqs.answer: a) Always true for any programming language
mcqs.explanation: It is always true as we have the facility of private and protected access specifiers. Also, only the public and global data are available globally or else the program should have proper permission to access the private data.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Polymorphism”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes polymorphism?

options.a: a) It is the ability for a message/data to be processed in more than one form
options.b: b) It is the ability for a message/data to be processed in only 1 form
options.c: c) It is the ability for many messages/data to be processed in one way
options.d: d) It is the ability for undefined message/data to be processed in at least one way

mcqs.answer: a) It is the ability for a message/data to be processed in more than one form
mcqs.explanation: It is actually the ability for a message / data to be processed in more than one form. The word polymorphism indicates many-forms. So if a single entity takes more than one form, it is known as polymorphism.

mcqs.question: What do you call the languages that support classes but not polymorphism?

options.d: d) If classes are supported, polymorphism will always be supported

mcqs.explanation: The languages which support classes but doesn’t support polymorphism, are known as object-based languages. Polymorphism is such an important feature, that is a language doesn’t support this feature, it can’t be called as a OOP language.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the language which supports classes but not polymorphism?
mcqs.explanation: Ada is the language which supports the concept of classes but doesn’t support the polymorphism feature. It is an object-based programming language. Note that it’s not an OOP language.

mcqs.question: If same message is passed to objects of several different classes and all of those can respond in a different way, what is this feature called?
mcqs.explanation: The feature defined in question defines polymorphism features. Here the different objects are capable of responding to the same message in different ways, hence polymorphism.

mcqs.question:
Which class/set of classes can illustrate polymorphism in the following code? 
abstract class student
{
   public : int marks;
   calc_grade();
}
class topper:public student
{
    public : calc_grade()
    { 
        return 10; 
    }
};
class average:public student
{ 
     public : calc_grade()
     {
         return 20; 
     }
};
class failed{ int marks; };

options.a: a) Only class student can show polymorphism
options.b: b) Only class student and topper together can show polymorphism
options.c: c) All class student, topper and average together can show polymorphism
options.d: d) Class failed should also inherit class student for this code to work for polymorphism

mcqs.answer: c) All class student, topper and average together can show polymorphism
mcqs.explanation: Since Student class is abstract class and class topper and average are inheriting student, class topper and average must define the function named calc_grade(); in abstract class. Since both the definition are different in those classes, calc_grade() will work in different way for same input from different objects. Hence it shows polymorphism.

mcqs.question: Which type of function among the following shows polymorphism?
mcqs.explanation: Only virtual functions among these can show polymorphism. Class member functions can show polymorphism too but we should be sure that the same function is being overloaded or is a function of abstract class or something like this, since we are not sure about all these, we can’t say whether it can show polymorphism or not.

mcqs.question: In case of using abstract class or function overloading, which function is supposed to be called first?

options.b: b) Function with highest priority in compiler
options.d: d) Function with lowest priority because it might have been halted since long time, because of low priority

mcqs.answer: b) Function with highest priority in compiler
mcqs.explanation: Function with highest priority is called. Here, it’s not about the thread scheduling in CPU, but it focuses on whether the function in local scope is present or not, or if scope resolution is used in some way, or if the function matches the argument signature. So all these things define which function has the highest priority to be called in runtime. Local function could be one of the answer but we can’t say if someone have used pointer to another function or same function name.

mcqs.question: Which among the following can’t be used for polymorphism?
mcqs.explanation: Static member functions are not property of any object. Hence it can’t be considered for overloading/overriding. For polymorphism, function must be property of object, not only of class.

mcqs.question:
What is output of the following program? 
class student
{ 
    public : int marks; 
	void disp() 
	{ 
		cout<<”its base class”
	};
	class topper:public student
	{
		public : 
		void disp()
		{ 
			cout<<”Its derived class”; 
		}
	}
	void main() { student s; topper t;
	s.disp();
	t.disp();
}

options.a: a) Its base classIts derived class
options.b: b) Its base class Its derived class
options.c: c) Its derived classIts base class
options.d: d) Its derived class Its base class

mcqs.answer: a) Its base classIts derived class
mcqs.explanation: You need to focus on how the output is going to be shown, no space will be given after first message from base class. And then the message from derived class will be printed. Function disp() in base class overrides the function of base class being derived.

mcqs.question: Which among the following can show polymorphism?
mcqs.explanation: Only insertion operator can be overloaded among all the given options. And the polymorphism can be illustrated here only if any of these is applicable of being overloaded. Overloading is type of polymorphism.

mcqs.question:
Find the output of the following program. 
class education
{ 
	char name[10];
	public : disp()
	{ 
		cout<<”Its education system”;
	}
	class school:public education
	{
		public: void dsip()
		{ 
			cout<<”Its school education system”;
		}
    };
	void main()
	{
                school s;
                s.disp();
	}
}

options.c: c) Its school education systemIts education system
options.d: d) Its education systemIts school education system

mcqs.explanation: Notice that the function name in derived class is different from the function name in base class. Hence when we call the disp() function, base class function is executed. No polymorphism is used here.

mcqs.question: Polymorphism is possible in C language.
mcqs.explanation: It is possible to implement polymorphism in C language, even though it doesn’t support class. We can use structures and then declare pointers which in turn points to some function. In this way we simulate the functions like member functions but not exactly member function. Now we can overload these functions, hence implementing polymorphism in C language.

mcqs.question: Which problem may arise if we use abstract class functions for polymorphism?

options.a: a) All classes are converted as abstract class
options.b: b) Derived class must be of abstract type
options.c: c) All the derived classes must implement the undefined functions
options.d: d) Derived classes can’t redefine the function

mcqs.answer: c) All the derived classes must implement the undefined functions
mcqs.explanation: The undefined functions must be defined is a problem, because one may need to implement few undefined functions from abstract class, but he will have to define each of the functions declared in abstract class. Being useless task, it is a problem sometimes.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is not true for polymorphism?

options.a: a) It is feature of OOP
options.b: b) Ease in readability of program
options.c: c) Helps in redefining the same functionality
options.d: d) Increases overhead of function definition always

mcqs.answer: d) Increases overhead of function definition always
mcqs.explanation: It never increases function definition overhead, one way or another if you don’t use polymorphism, you will use the definition in some other way, so it actually helps to write efficient codes.

mcqs.question: If 2 classes derive one base class and redefine a function of base class, also overload some operators inside class body. Among these two things of function and operator overloading, where is polymorphism used?

options.c: c) Both of these are using polymorphism
options.d: d) Either function overloading or operator overloading because polymorphism can be applied only once in a program

mcqs.answer: c) Both of these are using polymorphism
mcqs.explanation: Both of them are using polymorphism. It is not necessary that polymorphism can be used only once in a  program, it can be used anywhere, any number of times in a single program.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Encapsulation”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes encapsulation?

options.a: a) It is a way of combining various data members into a single unit
options.b: b) It is a way of combining various member functions into a single unit
options.c: c) It is a way of combining various data members and member functions into a single unit which can operate on any data
options.d: d) It is a way of combining various data members and member functions that operate on those data members into a single unit

mcqs.answer: d) It is a way of combining various data members and member functions that operate on those data members into a single unit
mcqs.explanation: It is a way of combining both data members and member functions, which operate on those data members, into a single unit. We call it a class in OOP generally. This feature have helped us modify the structures used in C language to be upgraded into class in C++ and other languages.

mcqs.question: If data members are private, what can we do to access them from the class object?

options.a: a) Create public member functions to access those data members
options.b: b) Create private member functions to access those data members
options.c: c) Create protected member functions to access those data members
options.d: d) Private data members can never be accessed from outside the class

mcqs.answer: a) Create public member functions to access those data members
mcqs.explanation: We can define public member functions to access those private data members and get their value for use or alteration. They can’t be accessed directly but is possible to be access using member functions. This is done to ensure that the private data doesn’t get modified accidentally.

mcqs.question: While using encapsulation, which among the following is possible?

options.a: a) Code modification can be additional overhead
options.b: b) Data member’s data type can be changed without changing any other code
options.c: c) Data member’s type can’t be changed, or whole code have to be changed
options.d: d) Member functions can be used to change the data type of data members

mcqs.answer: b) Data member’s data type can be changed without changing any other code
mcqs.explanation: Data member’s data type can be changed without changing any further code. All the members using that data can continue in the same way without any modification. Member functions can never change the data type of same class data members.

mcqs.question: Which feature can be implemented using encapsulation?
mcqs.explanation: Data abstraction can be achieved by using encapsulation. We can hide the operation and structure of actual program from the user and can show only required information by the user.

mcqs.question: Find which of the following uses encapsulation?

options.a: a) void main(){  int a;  void fun( int a=10;  cout<<a); fun(); }
options.b: b) class student{ int a;   public: int b;};
options.c: c) class student{int a; public: void disp(){ cout<<a;} };
options.d: d) struct topper{ char name[10]; public : int marks; }

mcqs.answer: c) class student{int a; public: void disp(){ cout<<a;} };
mcqs.explanation: It is the class which uses both the data members and member functions being declared inside a single unit. Only data members can be there in structures also. And the encapsulation can only be illustrated if some data/operations are associated within class.

mcqs.question: Encapsulation helps in writing ___________ classes in java.
mcqs.explanation: Immutable classes are used for caching purpose generally. And it can be created by making the class as final and making all its members private.

mcqs.question: Which among the following should be encapsulated?

options.a: a) The data which is prone to change is near future
options.b: b) The data prone to change in long terms
options.c: c) The data which is intended to be changed
options.d: d) The data which belongs to some other class

mcqs.answer: a) The data which is prone to change is near future
mcqs.explanation: The data prone to change in near future is usually encapsulated so that it doesn’t get changed accidentally. We encapsulate the data to hide the critical working of program from outside world.

mcqs.question: How can Encapsulation be achieved?
mcqs.explanation: Using access specifiers we can achieve encapsulation. Using this we can in turn implement data abstraction. It’s not necessary that we only use private access.

mcqs.question: Which among the following violates the principle of encapsulation almost always?
mcqs.explanation: Global variables almost always violates the principles of encapsulation. Encapsulation says the data should be accessed only by required set of elements. But global variable is accessible everywhere, also it is most prone to changes. It doesn’t hide the internal working of program.

mcqs.question: Which among the following would destroy the encapsulation mechanism if it was allowed in programming?

options.a: a) Using access declaration for private members of base class
options.b: b) Using access declaration for public members of base class
options.c: c) Using access declaration for local variable of main() function
options.d: d) Using access declaration for global variables

mcqs.answer: a) Using access declaration for private members of base class
mcqs.explanation: If using access declaration for private members of base class was allowed in programming, it would have destroyed whole concept of encapsulation. As if it was possible, any class which gets inherited privately, would have been able to inherit the private members of base class, and hence could access each and every member of base class.

mcqs.question: Which among the following can be a concept against encapsulation rules?

options.b: b) Using char* string pointer to be passed to non-member function
options.d: d) Using any kind of pointer/array address in passing to another function

mcqs.answer: d) Using any kind of pointer/array address in passing to another function
mcqs.explanation: If we use any kind of array or pointer as data member which should not be changed, but in some case its address is passed to some other function or similar variable. There are chances to modify its whole data easily. Hence Against encapsulation.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following code and select the correct option. 
class student
{  
     int marks;
     public : int* fun()
     { 
          return &marks; 
     }
};
main()
{
    student s;
    int *ptr=c.fun();
    return 0;
}

options.a: a) This code is good to go
options.b: b) This code may result in undesirable conditions
options.c: c) This code will generate error

mcqs.explanation: This code violates the encapsulation. By this code we can get the address of the private member of the class, hence we can change the value of private member, which is against the rules.

mcqs.question:
Consider the code and select the wrong choice. 
class hero
{ 
     char name[10];
     public : void disp()
     { 
          cout<<name;
     }
};

options.b: b) This code doesn’t maintain encapsulation

mcqs.explanation: This code maintains encapsulation. Here the private member is kept private. Outside code can’t access the private members of class. Only objects of this class will be able to access the public member function at maximum.

mcqs.question: Encapsulation is the way to add functions in a user defined structure.
mcqs.explanation: False, because we can’t call these structures if member functions are involved, it must be called class. Also, it is not just about adding functions, it’s about binding data and functions together.

mcqs.question: Using encapsulation data security is ___________
mcqs.explanation: The encapsulation can only ensure data security to some extent. If pointer and addresses are misused, it may violate encapsulation. Use of global variables also makes the program vulnerable, hence we can’t say that encapsulation gives pure security.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Abstraction”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best defines abstraction?

options.d: d) Hiding the implementation and showing only the features

mcqs.answer: d) Hiding the implementation and showing only the features
mcqs.explanation: It includes hiding the implementation part and showing only the required data and features to the user. It is done to hide the implementation complexity and details from the user. And to provide a good interface in programming.

mcqs.question: Hiding the implementation complexity can ____________

options.c: c) Provide more number of features

mcqs.explanation: It can make programming easy. The programming need not know how the inbuilt functions are working but can use those complex functions directly in the program. It doesn’t provide more number of features or better features.

mcqs.question: Class is _________ abstraction.
mcqs.explanation: Class is logical abstraction because it provides a logical structure for all of its objects. It gives an overview of the features of an object.

mcqs.question: Object is ________ abstraction.
mcqs.explanation: Object is real abstraction because it actually contains those features of class. It is the implementation of overview given by class. Hence the class is logical abstraction and its object is real.

mcqs.question: Abstraction gives higher degree of ________
mcqs.explanation: It is to idealize the interface. In this way the programmer can use the programming features more efficiently and can code better. It can’t increase the program complexity, as the feature itself is made to hide it.

mcqs.question: Abstraction can apply to ____________
mcqs.explanation: Abstraction applies to both. Control abstraction involves use of subroutines and control flow abstraction. Data abstraction involves handling pieces of data in meaningful ways.

mcqs.question: Which among the following can be viewed as combination of abstraction of data and code.
mcqs.explanation: Object can be viewed as abstraction of data and code. It uses data members and their functioning as data abstraction. Code abstraction as use of object of inbuilt class.

mcqs.question: Abstraction principle includes___________

options.a: a) Use abstraction at its minimum
options.b: b) Use abstraction to avoid longer codes
options.c: c) Use abstraction whenever possible to avoid duplication
options.d: d) Use abstraction whenever possible to achieve OOP

mcqs.answer: c) Use abstraction whenever possible to avoid duplication
mcqs.explanation: Abstraction principle includes use of abstraction to avoid duplication (usually of code). It this way the program doesn’t contain any redundant functions and make the program efficient.

mcqs.question: Higher the level of abstraction, higher are the details.
mcqs.explanation: Higher the level of abstraction, lower are the details. The best way to understand this is to consider a whole system that is highest level of abstraction as it hides everything inside. And next lower level would contain few of the computer components and so on.

mcqs.question: Encapsulation and abstraction differ as ____________

options.c: c) Can be used any way

mcqs.explanation: Abstraction is hiding the complex code. For example, we directly use cout object in C++ but we don’t know how is it actually implemented. Encapsulation is data binding, as in, we try to combine a similar type of data and functions together.

mcqs.question: In terms of stream and files ____________

options.a: a) Abstraction is called a stream and device is called a file
options.b: b) Abstraction is called a file and device is called a stream
options.c: c) Abstraction can be called both file and stream
options.d: d) Abstraction can’t be defined in terms of files and stream

mcqs.answer: a) Abstraction is called a stream and device is called a file
mcqs.explanation: Abstraction is called stream to provide a level of complexity hiding, for how the files operations are actually done. Actual devices are called file because in one way or another, those can be considered as single entity and there is nothing hidden.

mcqs.question: If two classes combine some private data members and provides public member functions to access and manipulate those data members. Where is abstraction used?

options.a: a) Using private access specifier for data members
options.b: b) Using class concept with both data members and member functions
options.c: c) Using public member functions to access and manipulate the data members
options.d: d) Data is not sufficient to decide what is being used

mcqs.answer: c) Using public member functions to access and manipulate the data members
mcqs.explanation: It is the concept of hiding program complexity and actual working in background. Hence use of public member functions illustrates abstraction here.

mcqs.question: A phone is made up of many components like motherboard, camera, sensors and etc. If the processor represents all the functioning of phone, display shows the display only, and the phone is represented as a whole. Which among the following have highest level of abstraction?
mcqs.explanation: Phone as a whole have the highest level of abstraction. This is because the phone being a single unit represents the whole system. Whereas motherboard, display and camera are its components.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is not a level of abstraction?
mcqs.explanation: Abstraction is generally divided into 3 different levels, namely, logical, physical and view level. External level is not defined in terms of abstraction.

mcqs.question: Using higher degree of abstraction __________
mcqs.explanation: It will make the code safer. One may think it reduces the readability, but the fact is, it actually helps us understand the code better. We don’t have to read the complex code which is of no use in understanding the program.

title: 2. OOPs MCQ on Constructors and Destructors

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Constructors”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is called first, automatically, whenever an object is created?
mcqs.explanation: Constructors are the member functions which are called automatically whenever an object is created. It is a mandatory functions to be called for an object to be created as this helps in initializing the object to a legal initial value for the class.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is not a necessary condition for constructors?

options.a: a) Its name must be same as that of class
options.b: b) It must not have any return type
options.c: c) It must contain a definition body

mcqs.answer: c) It must contain a definition body
mcqs.explanation: Constructors are predefined implicitly, even if the programmer doesn’t define any of them. Even if the programmer declares a constructor, it’s not necessary that it must contain some definition.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct?

options.a: a) class student{ public: int student(){} };
options.b: b) class student{ public: void student (){} };

mcqs.explanation: The constructors must not have any return type. Also, the body may or may not contain any body. Defining default constructor is optional, if you are not using any other constructor.

mcqs.question: In which access should a constructor be defined, so that object of the class can be created in any function?

options.d: d) Any access specifier will work

mcqs.explanation: Constructor function should be available to all the parts of program where the object is to be created. Hence it is advised to define it in public access, so that any other function is able to create objects.

mcqs.question: How many types of constructors are available for use in general (with respect to parameters)?
mcqs.explanation: Two types of constructors are defined generally, namely, default constructor and parameterized constructor. Default constructor is not necessary to be defined always.

mcqs.question: If a programmer defines a class and defines a default value parameterized constructor inside it. He has not defined any default constructor. And then he try to create the object without passing arguments, which among the following will be correct?

options.a: a) It will not create the object (as parameterized constructor is used)
options.b: b) It will create the object (as the default arguments are passed)
options.c: c) It will not create the object (as the default constructor is not defined)
options.d: d) It will create the object (as at least some constructor is defined)

mcqs.answer: b) It will create the object (as the default arguments are passed)
mcqs.explanation: It will create the object without any problem, because the default arguments use the default value if no value is passed. Hence it is equal to default constructor with zero parameters. But it will not create the object if signature doesn’t match.

mcqs.question: Default constructor must be defined, if parameterized constructor is defined and the object is to be created without arguments.
mcqs.explanation: If the object is create without arguments and only parameterized constructors are used, compiler will give an error as there is no default constructor defined. And some constructor must be called so as to create an object in memory.

mcqs.question: If class C inherits class B. And B has inherited class A. Then while creating the object of class C, what will be the sequence of constructors getting called?

options.a: a) Constructor of C then B, finally of A
options.b: b) Constructor of A then C, finally of B
options.c: c) Constructor of C then A, finally B
options.d: d) Constructor of A then B, finally C

mcqs.answer: d) Constructor of A then B, finally C
mcqs.explanation: While creating the object of class C, its constructor would be called by default. But, if the class is inheriting some other class, firstly the parent class constructor will be called so that all the data is initialized that is being inherited.

mcqs.question:
In multiple inheritance, if class C inherits two classes A and B as follows, which class constructor will be called first? 
class A{ };
class B{ };
class C: public A, public B{  };
mcqs.explanation: Constructor of class A will be called first. This is because the constructors in multiple inheritance are called in the sequence in which they are written to be inherited. Here A is written first, hence it is called first.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true for copy constructor?

options.a: a) The argument object is passed by reference
options.b: b) It can be defined with zero arguments
options.c: c) Used when an object is passed by value to a function
options.d: d) Used when a function returns an object

mcqs.answer: b) It can be defined with zero arguments
mcqs.explanation: It can’t be defined with zero number of arguments. This is because to copy one object to another, the object must be mentioned so that compiler can take values from that object.

mcqs.question: If the object is passed by value to a copy constructor?

options.a: a) Only public members will be accessible to be copied
options.c: c) Compiler will give out of memory error
options.d: d) Data stored in data members won’t be accessible

mcqs.answer: c) Compiler will give out of memory error
mcqs.explanation: Compiler runs out of memory. This is because while passing the argument by value, a constructor of the object will be called. That in turn called another object constructor for values, and this goes on. This is like a constructor call to itself, and this goes on infinite times, hence it must be passed by reference, so that the constructor is not called.

mcqs.question:
Which object will be created first? 
class student 
{  
    int marks;
};
student s1, s2, s3;

options.a: a) s1 then s2 then s3
options.b: b) s3 then s2 then s1
options.c: c) s2 then s3 then s1
options.d: d) all are created at same time

mcqs.answer: a) s1 then s2 then s3
mcqs.explanation: The objects are created in the sequence of how they are written. This happens because the constructors are called in the sequence of how the objects are mentioned. This is done in sequence.

mcqs.question: Which among the following helps to create a temporary instance?

options.a: a) Implicit call to a default constructor
options.b: b) Explicit call to a copy constructor
options.c: c) Implicit call to a parameterized constructor
options.d: d) Explicit call to a constructor

mcqs.answer: d) Explicit call to a constructor
mcqs.explanation:
Explicit call to a constructor can let you create a temporary instance. This is because the temporary instances doesn’t have any name. Those are deleted from memory as soon as their reference is removed.

Implicit calls: The compiler might implicitly call a default constructor (if available) when you declare an object without arguments. However, these are not temporary instances as they are assigned to a variable.

Explicit calls: You explicitly use the new keyword followed by the constructor name and arguments to create a new object. This is the most common way to create temporary objects.

Copy constructors: These constructors are used to create a copy of an existing object. They are not typically used for temporary instances.

Therefore, only an explicit call to a constructor allows you to create a temporary instance that isn’t assigned to a variable and exists momentarily within the expression or statement.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is correct for the class defined below? 
class student
{
    int marks;
    public: student(){}
    student(int x)
    { 
         marks=x; 
    }
};
main()
{
    student s1(100);
    student s2();
    student s3=100;
    return 0;
}

options.b: b) Only object s1 and s2 will be created
options.c: c) Program runs and all objects are created
options.d: d) Program will give compile time error

mcqs.answer: c) Program runs and all objects are created
mcqs.explanation: It is a special case of constructor with only 1 argument. While calling a constructor with one argument, you are actually implicitly creating a conversion from the argument type to the type of class. Hence you can directly specify the value of that one argument with assignment operator.

mcqs.question: For constructor overloading, each constructor must differ in ___________ and __________

options.a: a) Number of arguments and type of arguments
options.b: b) Number of arguments and return type
options.c: c) Return type and type of arguments

mcqs.answer: a) Number of arguments and type of arguments
mcqs.explanation: Each constructor must differ in the number of arguments it accepts and the type of arguments. This actually defines the constructor signature. This helps to remove the ambiguity and define a unique constructor as required.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Types of Constructors”.

mcqs.question: How many types of constructors are available, in general, in any language?
mcqs.explanation: There are 3 types of constructors in general, namely, default constructors, parameterized constructors and copy constructors. Default one is called whenever an object is created without arguments.

mcqs.question:
Choose the correct option for the following code. 
class student
{
    int marks;
}
student s1;
student s2=2;

options.a: a) Object s1 should be passed with argument
options.b: b) Object s2 should not be declared
options.c: c) Object s2 will not be created, but program runs
options.d: d) Program gives compile time error

mcqs.answer: d) Program gives compile time error
mcqs.explanation: The object s2 can be assigned with one value only if a single argument constructor is defined in class, but here, it can’t be done as no constructor is defined. Hence every object must be declare or created without using arguments.

mcqs.question: Which constructor is called while assigning some object with another?
mcqs.explanation: Copy constructor is used while an object is assigned with another. This is mandatory since we can’t decide which member should be assigned to which member value. By using copy constructor, we can assign the values in required form.

mcqs.question: It’s necessary to pass object by reference in copy constructor because ____________

options.a: a) Constructor is not called in pass by reference
options.b: b) Constructor is called in pass by reference only
options.c: c) It passes the address of new constructor to be created
options.d: d) It passes the address of new object to be created

mcqs.answer: a) Constructor is not called in pass by reference
mcqs.explanation: Object must be passed by reference to copy constructor because constructor is not called in pass by reference. Otherwise, in pass by value, a temporary object will be created which in turn will try to call its constructor that is already being used. This results in creating infinite number of objects and hence memory shortage error will be shown.

mcqs.question: Which specifier applies only to the constructors?
mcqs.explanation: The keyword explicit can be used while defining the constructor only. This is used to suppress the implicit call to the constructor. It ensures that the constructors are being called with the default syntax only (i.e. only by using object and constructor name).

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) Default constructor can’t be defined by the programmer
options.b: b) Default parameters constructor isn’t equivalent to the default constructor
options.c: c) Default constructor can be called explicitly
options.d: d) Default constructor is and always called implicitly only

mcqs.answer: c) Default constructor can be called explicitly
mcqs.explanation: Default constructors can be called explicitly anytime. They are specifically used to allocate memory space for the object in memory, in general. It is not necessary that these should always be called implicitly.

mcqs.question: Which type of constructor can’t have a return type?

options.d: d) Constructors don’t have a return type

mcqs.answer: d) Constructors don’t have a return type
mcqs.explanation: Constructors don’t return any value. Those are special functions, whose return type is not defined, not even void. This is so because the constructors are meant to initialize the members of class and not to perform some task which can return some value to newly created object.

mcqs.question: Why do we use static constructors?

options.a: a) To initialize the static members of class
options.b: b) To initialize all the members with static value
options.c: c) To delete the static members when not required
options.d: d) To clear all the static members initialized values

mcqs.answer: a) To initialize the static members of class
mcqs.explanation: Static constructors help in initializing the static members of the class. This is provided because the static members are not considered to be property of the object, rather they are considered as the property of class.

mcqs.question: When and how many times a static constructor is called?

options.a: a) Created at time of object destruction
options.b: b) Called at first time when an object is created and only one time
options.c: c) Called at first time when an object is created and called with every new object creation
options.d: d) Called whenever an object go out of scope

mcqs.answer: b) Called at first time when an object is created and only one time
mcqs.explanation: Those are called at very first call of object creation. That is called only one time because the value of static members must be retained and continued from the time it gets created.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true for static constructor?

options.a: a) Static constructors are called with every new object
options.b: b) Static constructors are used initialize data members to zero always
options.c: c) Static constructors can’t be parameterized constructors
options.d: d) Static constructors can be used to initialize the non-static members also

mcqs.answer: c) Static constructors can’t be parameterized constructors
mcqs.explanation: Static constructors can’t be parameterized constructors. Those are used to initialize the value of static members only. And that must be a definite value. Accepting arguments may make it possible that static members loses their value with every new object being created.

mcqs.question: Within a class, only one static constructor can be created.
mcqs.explanation: Since the static constructors are can’t be parameterized, they can’t be overloaded. Having this case, only one constructor will be possible to be created in a local scope, because the signature will always be same and hence it will not be possible to overload static constructor.

mcqs.question: Default constructor initializes all data members as ___________

options.a: a) All numeric member with some garbage values and string to random string
options.b: b) All numeric member with some garbage values and string to null
options.c: c) All numeric member with zero and strings to random value
options.d: d) All numeric member with zero and strings to null

mcqs.answer: d) All numeric member with zero and strings to null
mcqs.explanation: Default constructor, which even the programmer doesn’t define, always initialize the values as zero if numeric and null if string. This is done so as to avoid the accidental values to change the conditional statements being used and similar conditions.

mcqs.question: When is the static constructor called?

options.a: a) After the first instance is created
options.b: b) Before default constructor call of first instance
options.c: c) Before first instance is created
options.d: d) At time of creation of first instance

mcqs.answer: c) Before first instance is created
mcqs.explanation: The static constructor is called before creation of the first instance of that class. This is done so that even the first instance can use the static value of the static members of the class and manipulate as required.

mcqs.question: If constructors of a class are defined in private access, then __________

options.a: a) The class can’t be inherited
options.b: b) The class can be inherited
options.c: c) Instance can be created only in another class
options.d: d) Instance can be created anywhere in the program

mcqs.answer: a) The class can’t be inherited
mcqs.explanation: If the constructors are defined in private access, then the class can’t be inherited by other classes. This is useful when the class contains static members only. The instances can never be created.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is correct, based on the given code below? 
class student
{ 
     int marks;
     public : student()
     {  
          cout<<”New student details can be added now”;
     }
};
student s1;

options.a: a) Cout can’t be used inside the constructor
options.b: b) Constructor must contain only initializations

mcqs.explanation: This program will work fine. This is because it is not mandatory that a constructor must contain only initialization only. If you want to perform a task on each instance being created, that code can be written inside the constructor.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Copy Constructor”.

mcqs.question: Copy constructor is a constructor which ________________

options.a: a) Creates an object by copying values from any other object of same class
options.b: b) Creates an object by copying values from first object created for that class
options.c: c) Creates an object by copying values from another object of another class
options.d: d) Creates an object by initializing it with another previously created object of same class

mcqs.answer: d) Creates an object by initializing it with another previously created object of same class
mcqs.explanation: The object that has to be copied to new object must be previously created. The new object gets initialized with the same values as that of the object mentioned for being copied. The exact copy is made with values.

mcqs.question: The copy constructor can be used to ____________

options.a: a) Initialize one object from another object of same type
options.b: b) Initialize one object from another object of different type
options.c: c) Initialize more than one object from another object of same type at a time
options.d: d) Initialize all the objects of a class to another object of another class

mcqs.answer: a) Initialize one object from another object of same type
mcqs.explanation: The copy constructor has the most basic function to initialize the members of an object with same values as that of some previously created object. The object must be of same class.

mcqs.question: If two classes have exactly same data members and member function and only they differ by class name. Can copy constructor be used to initialize one class object with another class object?

options.b: b) Yes, because the members are same
options.d: d) No, but possible if constructor is also same

mcqs.explanation: The restriction for copy constructor is that it must be used with the object of same class. Even if the classes are exactly same the constructor won’t be able to access all the members of another class. Hence we can’t use object of another class for initialization.

mcqs.question: The copy constructors can be used to ________

options.a: a) Copy an object so that it can be passed to a class
options.b: b) Copy an object so that it can be passed to a function
options.c: c) Copy an object so that it can be passed to another primitive type variable
options.d: d) Copy an object for type casting

mcqs.answer: b) Copy an object so that it can be passed to a function
mcqs.explanation: When an object is passed to a function, actually its copy is made in the function. To copy the values, copy constructor is used. Hence the object being passed and object being used in function are different.

mcqs.question: Which returning an object, we can use ____________
mcqs.explanation: While returning an object we can use the copy constructor. When we assign the return value to another object of same class then this copy constructor will be used. And all the members will be assigned the same values as that of the object being returned.

mcqs.question: If programmer doesn’t define any copy constructor then _____________

options.a: a) Compiler provides an implicit copy constructor
options.c: c) The objects can’t be assigned with another objects
options.d: d) The program gives run time error if copying is used

mcqs.answer: a) Compiler provides an implicit copy constructor
mcqs.explanation: The compiler provides an implicit copy constructor. It is not mandatory to always create an explicit copy constructor. The values are copied using implicit constructor only.

mcqs.question: If a class implements some dynamic memory allocations and pointers then _____________

options.a: a) Copy constructor must be defined
options.b: b) Copy constructor must not be defined
options.c: c) Copy constructor can’t be defined
options.d: d) Copy constructor will not be used

mcqs.answer: a) Copy constructor must be defined
mcqs.explanation: In the case where dynamic memory allocation is used, the copy constructor definition must be given. The implicit copy constructor is not capable of manipulating the dynamic memory and pointers. Explicit definition allows to manipulate the data as required.

mcqs.question: What is the syntax of copy constructor?
mcqs.explanation: The syntax must contain the class name first, followed by the classname as type and &object within parenthesis. Then comes the constructor body. The definition can be given as per requirements.

mcqs.question: Object being passed to a copy constructor ___________

options.a: a) Must be passed by reference
options.b: b) Must be passed by value
options.c: c) Must be passed with integer type
options.d: d) Must not be mentioned in parameter list

mcqs.answer: a) Must be passed by reference
mcqs.explanation: This is mandatory to pass the object by reference. Otherwise, the object will try to create another object to copy its values, in turn a constructor will be called, and this will keep on calling itself. This will cause the compiler to give out of memory error.

mcqs.question: Out of memory error is given when the object _____________ to the copy constructor.

options.d: d) Is not passed by reference

mcqs.answer: d) Is not passed by reference
mcqs.explanation: All the options given, directly or indirectly indicate that the object is being passed by reference. And if object is not passed by reference then the out of memory error is produced. Due to infinite constructor call of itself.

mcqs.question: Copy constructor will be called whenever the compiler __________
mcqs.explanation: Whenever the compiler creates a temporary object, copy constructor is used to copy the values from existing object to the temporary object.

mcqs.question: The deep copy is possible only with the help of __________
mcqs.explanation: While using explicit copy constructor, the pointers of copied object point to the intended memory location. This is assured since the programmers themselves manipulate the addresses.

mcqs.question: Can a copy constructor be made private?

options.b: b) Yes, if no other constructor is defined
options.d: d) No, private members can’t be accessed

mcqs.explanation: The copy constructor can be defined as private. If we make it private then the objects of the class can’t be copied. It can be used when a class used dynamic memory allocation.

mcqs.question: The arguments to a copy constructor _____________
mcqs.explanation: The object should not be modified in the copy constructor. Because the object itself is being copied. When the object is returned from a function, the object must be a constant otherwise the compiler creates a temporary object which can die anytime.

mcqs.question: Copy constructors are overloaded constructors.
mcqs.explanation: The copy constructors are always overloaded constructors. They have to be. All the classes have a default constructor and other constructors are basically overloaded constructors.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Overloading Constructors”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes constructor overloading?

options.a: a) Defining one constructor in each class of a program
options.b: b) Defining more than one constructor in single class
options.c: c) Defining more than one constructor in single class with different signature
options.d: d) Defining destructor with each constructor

mcqs.answer: c) Defining more than one constructor in single class with different signature
mcqs.explanation: If more than one constructors are defined in a class with same signature, then that results in error. The signatures must be different. So that the constructors can be differentiated.

mcqs.question: Can constructors be overloaded in derived class?

options.b: b) Yes, if derived class has no constructor
options.c: c) No, programmer can’t do it

mcqs.explanation: The constructor must be having the same name as that of a class. Hence a constructor of one class can’t even be defined in another class. Since the constructors can’t be defined in derived class, it can’t be overloaded too, in derived class.

mcqs.question: Does constructor overloading include different return types for constructors to be overloaded?

options.a: a) Yes, if return types are different, signature becomes different
options.b: b) Yes, because return types can differentiate two functions
options.c: c) No, return type can’t differentiate two functions
options.d: d) No, constructors doesn’t have any return type

mcqs.answer: d) No, constructors doesn’t have any return type
mcqs.explanation: The constructors doesn’t have any return type. When we can’t have return type of a constructor, overloading based on the return type is not possible. Hence only parameters can be different.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is possible way to overload constructor?

options.a: a) Define default constructor, 1 parameter constructor and 2 parameter constructor
options.b: b) Define default constructor, zero argument constructor and 1 parameter constructor
options.c: c) Define default constructor, and 2 other parameterized constructors with same signature

mcqs.answer: a) Define default constructor, 1 parameter constructor and 2 parameter constructor
mcqs.explanation: All the constructors defined in a class must have a different signature in order to be overloaded. Here one default and other parameterized constructors are used, wherein one is of only one parameter and other accepts two. Hence overloading is possible.

mcqs.question:
Which constructor will be called from the object created in the code below? 
class A
{ 
	int i;
	A()
	{ 
		i=0; cout<<i; 
	}
	A(int x=0)
	{ 
		i=x;  cout<<I;  
	}
};
A obj1;
mcqs.explanation: When a default constructor is defined and another constructor with 1 default value argument is defined, creating object without parameter will create ambiguity for the compiler. The compiler won’t be able to decide which constructor should be called, hence compile time error.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is false for a constructor?

options.a: a) Constructors doesn’t have a return value
options.b: b) Constructors are always user defined
options.c: c) Constructors are overloaded with different signature
options.d: d) Constructors may or may not have any arguments being accepted

mcqs.answer: b) Constructors are always user defined
mcqs.explanation: The constructors are not always user defined. The construct will be provided implicitly from the compiler if the used doesn’t defined any constructor. The implicit constructor makes all the string values null and allocates memory space for each data member.

mcqs.question: When is the constructor called for an object?

options.a: a) As soon as overloading is required
options.b: b) As soon as class is derived
options.c: c) As soon as class is created
options.d: d) As soon as object is created

mcqs.answer: d) As soon as object is created
mcqs.explanation: The constructor is called as soon as the object is created. The overloading comes into picture as to identify which constructor have to be called depending on arguments passed in the creation of object.

mcqs.question: Which among the following function can be used to call default constructor implicitly in java?
mcqs.explanation: The function this() can be used to call the default constructor from inside any other constructor. This helps to further reuse the code and not to write the redundant data in all the constructors.

mcqs.question: Why do we use constructor overloading?

options.a: a) To use different types of constructors
options.b: b) Because it’s a feature provided
options.c: c) To initialize the object in different ways
options.d: d) To differentiate one constructor from another

mcqs.answer: c) To initialize the object in different ways
mcqs.explanation: The constructors are overloaded to initialize the objects of a class in different ways. This allows us to initialize the object with either default values or used given values. If data members are not initialized then program may give unexpected results.

mcqs.question: If programmer have defined parameterized constructor only, then __________________

options.a: a) Default constructor will not be created by the compiler implicitly
options.b: b) Default constructor will be created by the compiler implicitly
options.c: c) Default constructor will not be created but called at runtime

mcqs.answer: a) Default constructor will not be created by the compiler implicitly
mcqs.explanation: When the programmer doesn’t specify any default constructor and only defines some parameterized constructor. The compiler doesn’t provide any default constructor implicitly. This is because it is assumed that the programmer will create the objects only with constructors.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is not valid in java?
mcqs.explanation: Java doesn’t provide the feature to recursively call the constructor. This is to eliminate the out of memory error in some cases that arises unexpectedly. That is an predefined condition for constructors in java.

mcqs.question:
Which constructor will be called from the object obj2 in the following program? 
class A
{
	int i;
	A()
	{  
		i=0;  
	}
	A(int x)
	{  
		i=x+1;  
	}
	A(int y, int x)
	{  
		i=x+y;  
	}
};
A obj1(10);
A obj2(10,20);
A obj3;
mcqs.explanation: The two argument constructor will be called as we are passing 2 arguments to the object while creation. The arguments will be passed together and hence compiler resolves that two argument constructor have to be called.

mcqs.question: What are we only create an object but don’t call any constructor for it in java?

options.a: a) Implicit constructor will be called
options.b: b) Object is initialized to some null values
options.d: d) Object is created but points to null

mcqs.answer: d) Object is created but points to null
mcqs.explanation: The object becomes a reference object which can be initialized will another object. Then this object will indirectly become another name of the object being assigned. If not assigned, it simply points to null address.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is false?

options.a: a) Constructor can’t be overloaded in Kotlin
options.b: b) Constructors can’t be called recursively in java
options.c: c) Constructors can be overloaded in C++
options.d: d) Constructors overloading depends on different signatures

mcqs.answer: a) Constructor can’t be overloaded in Kotlin
mcqs.explanation: Kotlin language allows constructor overloading. This is a basic feature for the constructors. The constructor overloading allows the object to be initialized according to the user.

mcqs.question: Which is correct syntax?
mcqs.explanation: The syntax for object creating in java with calling a constructor for is it is as in option c. The syntax must contain the classname followed by the object name. The keyword new must be used and then the constructor call with or without the parameters as required.

links.text: OOPs MCQ: Execution of Constructor or Destructor
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Execution of Constructor or Destructor”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes the constructors?

options.a: a) A function which is called whenever an object is referenced
options.b: b) A function which is called whenever an object is created to initialize the members
options.c: c) A function which is called whenever an object is assigned to copy the values
