options.d: d) A function which is called whenever an object is to be given values for members

mcqs.answer: b) A function which is called whenever an object is created to initialize the members
mcqs.explanation: The constructors are special type of functions which are called whenever an object is created. This is to initialize the data members of the class. The constructor allocates memory space for all the data members.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes destructor?

options.a: a) A function which is called just before the objects are destroyed
options.b: b) A function which is called after each reference to the object
options.c: c) A function which is called after termination of the program
options.d: d) A function which is called before calling any member function

mcqs.answer: a) A function which is called just before the objects are destroyed
mcqs.explanation: The Destructors are special functions which are called just before an object is destroyed. This functions is responsible to free all the allocated resources to the object. Objects are destroyed whenever those go out of scope.

mcqs.question: Which among the following represents correct constructor?
mcqs.explanation: The constructors must contain only the class name. The class name is followed by the blank parenthesis or we can have parameters if some values are to be passed.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct syntax for the destructors?
mcqs.explanation: The destructor must have same name as that of the corresponding class. The class name should be preceded by the tilde symbol (~).

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) First the constructor of parent classes are called in sequence of inheritance
options.b: b) First the constructor of child classes are called in the sequence of inheritance
options.c: c) First constructor called is of the object being created

mcqs.answer: a) First the constructor of parent classes are called in sequence of inheritance
mcqs.explanation: First the constructor of parent class are called. The order in which the parent class constructors are called is same in the sequence of inheritance used.

mcqs.question: What is the sequence of destructors call?

options.a: a) Same order as that of the constructors call
options.d: d) Revere of the order of constructor call

mcqs.answer: d) Revere of the order of constructor call
mcqs.explanation: The destructors are called in the reverse order as that of the constructors being called. This is done to ensure that all the resources are released in sequence. That is, the derived class destructors will be called first.

mcqs.question: The destructors _____________________

options.a: a) Can have maximum one argument
options.c: c) Can have more than one argument
options.d: d) Can’t have more than 3 arguments

mcqs.explanation: The destructors doesn’t have any arguments. The destructors have to be called implicitly whenever an object goes out of scope. The user can’t pass argument to the implicit call.

mcqs.question: Destructor calls ________________ (C++)

options.c: c) Can be implicit or explicit
options.d: d) Are made at end of program only

mcqs.answer: c) Can be implicit or explicit
mcqs.explanation: The destructors are usually called implicitly whenever an object goes out of scope. The destructors can also be called explicitly if required. The call must be made, implicitly or explicitly.

mcqs.question: Number of destructors called are ____________

options.a: a) Always equal to number of constructors called
options.b: b) Always less than the number of constructors called
options.c: c) Always greater than the number of constructors called
options.d: d) Always less than or equal to number of constructors

mcqs.answer: a) Always equal to number of constructors called
mcqs.explanation: Destructor will be called only to free the resources allocated for an object. The resources are allocated only the constructor for an object is called.

mcqs.question: For explicit call _________________

options.a: a) The destructor must be private
options.b: b) The destructor must be public
options.c: c) The destructor must be protected
options.d: d) The destructor must be defined outside the class

mcqs.answer: b) The destructor must be public
mcqs.explanation: The destructor must be public for explicit calls. If it is made private or protected then it won’t be accessible outside the class. There is no restriction of definition the destructor outside the class.

mcqs.question: If a class have 4 constructors then it must have 4 destructors also.
mcqs.explanation: Even if the class have 4 constructors, only one would be used. And only one destructor is allowed.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true for destructors?

options.b: b) Destructors can be define more than one time
options.d: d) Destructors are overloaded in derived classes

mcqs.explanation: The destructors can never be overloaded. The destructors doesn’t have arguments. And to get overloaded, they must have different signature. This is not possible if arguments are not allowed.

mcqs.question: The constructor _____________

options.b: b) May have a return type
options.c: c) Of derived classes have return type
options.d: d) Doesn’t have a return type

mcqs.answer: d) Doesn’t have a return type
mcqs.explanation: The constructors doesn’t have any return type. The constructors are intended to allocate the resources for the object. Memory spaces are to be finalized.

mcqs.question: The destructors ____________

options.b: b) May have a return type
options.c: c) Of derived classes have return type
options.d: d) Doesn’t have a return type

mcqs.answer: d) Doesn’t have a return type
mcqs.explanation: The destructors are intended to free the memory space. And all the resources that were allocated for the object. The return value is not supported since only memory has to be made free.

mcqs.question: The destructor can be called before the constructor if required.
mcqs.explanation: The destructors can be called only after the constructor calls. It is not a mandatory rule but the deletion can only take place if there is something created using the constructor.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on ” Destructors”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following describes a destructor?

options.a: a) A special function that is called to free the resources, acquired by the object
options.b: b) A special function that is called to delete the class
options.c: c) A special function that is called anytime to delete an object
options.d: d) A special function that is called to delete all the objects of a class

mcqs.answer: a) A special function that is called to free the resources, acquired by the object
mcqs.explanation: It is used to free the resources that the object might had used in its lifespan. The destructors are called implicitly whenever an object’s life ends.

mcqs.question: When a destructor is called?

options.a: a) After the end of object life
options.b: b) Anytime in between object’s lifespan
options.c: c) At end of whole program
options.d: d) Just before the end of object life

mcqs.answer: d) Just before the end of object life
mcqs.explanation: The destructor is called just before the object go out of scope or just before its life ends. This is done to ensure that all the resources reserved for the object are used and at last, are made free for others.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct for abstract class destructors?

options.c: c) It may or may not have destructors
options.d: d) It contains an implicit destructor

mcqs.explanation: It doesn’t have destructors. Since an abstract class don’t have constructors, and hence can’t have instances. Having this case, the abstract classes don’t have destructors too, because that would be of no use here.

mcqs.question: If in multiple inheritance, class C inherits class B, and Class B inherits class A. In which sequence are their destructors called if an object of class C was declared?
mcqs.explanation: The destructors are always called in the reverse order of how the constructors were called. Here class A constructor would have been created first if Class C object is declared. Hence class A destructor is called at last.

mcqs.question:
Choose the correct sequence of destructors being called for the following code. 
class A{   };
class B{   };
class C: public A, public B{   };
mcqs.explanation: In multiple inheritance, the constructors are called in the sequence of how they are written in inheritance sequence. And the destructors will be called in the reverse order. This can be cross verified just by printing a message from each destructor defined in classes.

mcqs.question: When is the destructor of a global object called?

options.a: a) Just before end of program
options.b: b) Just after end of program
options.c: c) With the end of program
options.d: d) Anytime when object is not needed

mcqs.answer: a) Just before end of program
mcqs.explanation: This is because the lifespan of global object is from start of the program, till the end of the program. And hence program end is the end of global object too. Just before the end of program, the destructor will be called to free the acquired resources by the objects.

mcqs.question: How the constructors and destructors can be differentiated?

options.a: a) Destructor have a return type but constructor doesn’t
options.b: b) Destructors can’t be defined by the programmer, but constructors can be defined
options.c: c) Destructors are preceded with a tilde (~) symbol, and constructor doesn’t
options.d: d) Destructors are same as constructors in syntax

mcqs.answer: c) Destructors are preceded with a tilde (~) symbol, and constructor doesn’t
mcqs.explanation: The destructors are preceded with the tilde (~) symbol. The name is same as that of the class. These also doesn’t have any return type.

mcqs.question: Destructors doesn’t accept parameters.
mcqs.explanation: The destructors doesn’t accept the arguments. Those are just used to free up the resources.

mcqs.question: Destructors can be ________

options.d: d) Any type depending on situation

mcqs.explanation: The destructors can be virtual. It is actually advised to keep the destructors virtual always. This is done to suppress the problems that may arise if inheritance is involved.

mcqs.question: Global destructors execute in ___________ order after main function is terminated.
mcqs.explanation: The destructors are always called in reverse order no matter which destructor it is. This is done to ensure that all the resources are able to get free. And no resource is kept busy.

mcqs.question: When is it advised to have user defined destructor?

options.a: a) When class contains some pointer to memory allocated in class
options.b: b) When a class contains static variables
options.c: c) When a class contains static functions
options.d: d) When a class is inheriting another class only

mcqs.answer: a) When class contains some pointer to memory allocated in class
mcqs.explanation: This is always advised to have user defined destructor when pointers are involved in class. This is usually done to ensure that the memory, that was allocated dynamically, gets free after use and doesn’t cause memory leak.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct for the destructors concept?

options.b: b) Destructors can have only one parameter at maximum
options.c: c) Destructors are always called after object goes out of scope
options.d: d) There can be only one destructor in a class

mcqs.answer: d) There can be only one destructor in a class
mcqs.explanation: This is so because the destructors can’t be overloaded. And the destructor must have the same name as that of class with a tilde symbol preceding the name of the destructor. Hence there can be only one destructor in a class. Since more than one function with same name and signature can’t be present in same scope.

mcqs.question:
Which class destructor will be called first, when following code go out of scope? 
class A{  };
class B{  };
class C: public B{  };
A a;
B b;
C c;
mcqs.explanation: The constructor that would have created at last, its destructor will be called first when the code goes out of scope. This will help the program to manage the resources more efficiently.

mcqs.question: When an object is passed to a function, its copy is made in the function and then ______________

options.a: a) The destructor of the copy is called when function is returned
options.b: b) The destructor is never called in this case
options.c: c) The destructor is called but it is always implicit
options.d: d) The destructor must be user defined

mcqs.answer: a) The destructor of the copy is called when function is returned
mcqs.explanation: When an object is passed to a function, its copy is made in the function. This copy acts as a real object till the function is live. When the function is returned, the copy’s destructor is called to free the resources held by it.

mcqs.question: What happens when an object is passed by reference?

options.b: b) Destructor is called at end of function
options.c: c) Destructor is called when function is out of scope
options.d: d) Destructor is called when called explicitly

mcqs.explanation: The destructor is never called in this situation. The concept is that when an object is passed by reference to the function, the constructor is not called, but only the main object will be used. Hence no destructor will be called at end of function.

title: 3. Object Oriented Programming MCQ on Access Specifiers

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Access Specifiers”.

mcqs.question: How many types of access specifiers are provided in OOP (C++)?
mcqs.explanation: Only 3 types of access specifiers are available. Namely, private, protected and public. All these three can be used according to the need of security of members.

mcqs.question: Which among the following can be used together in a single class?
mcqs.explanation: All the classes can use any of the specifiers as needed. There is no restriction on how many of them can be used together.

mcqs.question: Which among the following can restrict class members to get inherited?
mcqs.explanation: Private members of a class can’t be inherited. These members can only be accessible from members of its own class only. It is used to secure the data.

mcqs.question: Which access specifier is used when no access specifier is used with a member of class (java)?
mcqs.explanation: Default access is used if the programmer doesn’t specify the specifier. This acts in a similar way as that of private. But since nothing is specified we call it to default access.

mcqs.question: Which specifier allows a programmer to make the private members which can be inherited?
mcqs.explanation: Protected access is used to make the members private. But those members can be inherited. This gives both security and code reuse capability to a program.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is false?

options.a: a) Private members can be accessed using friend functions
options.b: b) Member functions can be made private
options.c: c) Default members can’t be inherited
options.d: d) Public members are accessible from other classes also

mcqs.answer: c) Default members can’t be inherited
mcqs.explanation: The default members can be inherited. Provided that they are in same package. It works in a little different way from private access specifier.

mcqs.question: If a class has all the private members, which specifier will be used for its implicit constructor?
mcqs.explanation: The implicit constructor will always be public. Otherwise the class wouldn’t be able to have instances. In turn, no objects will be created and the class can only be used for inheritance.

mcqs.question: If class A has add() function with protected access, and few other members in public. Then class B inherits class A privately. Will the user will not be able to call _________ from the object of class B.

options.a: a) Any function of class A
options.b: b) The add() function of class A
options.c: c) Any member of class A
options.d: d) Private, protected and public members of class A

mcqs.answer: d) Private, protected and public members of class A
mcqs.explanation: Class B object will not be able to call any of the private, protected and public members of class A. It is not only about the function add(), but all the members of class A will become private members of class B.

mcqs.question: Which access specifier should be used in a class where the instances can’t be created?

options.c: c) Only default constructor to be public
options.d: d) Only default constructor to be protected

mcqs.explanation: All the constructors must be made private. This will restrict the instance of class to be made anywhere in the program. Since the constructors are private, no instance will be able to call them and hence won’t be allocated with any memory space.

mcqs.question: On which specifier’s data, does the size of a class’s object depend?

options.a: a) All the data members are added
options.b: b) Only private members are added
options.c: c) Only public members are added
options.d: d) Only default data members are added

mcqs.answer: a) All the data members are added
mcqs.explanation: All the data members are counted to calculate the size of an object of a class. The data member access specifier doesn’t play any role here. Hence all the data size will be added.

mcqs.question: If class B inherits class A privately. And class B has a friend function. Will the friend function be able to access the private member of class A?

options.a: a) Yes, because friend function can access all the members
options.b: b) Yes, because friend function is of class B
options.c: c) No, because friend function can only access private members of friend class
options.d: d) No, because friend function can access private member of class A also

mcqs.answer: c) No, because friend function can only access private members of friend class
mcqs.explanation: The friend function of class B will not be able to access private members of class A. Since B is inheriting class A privately, the members will become private in class B. But private members of class A won’t be inherited at all. Hence it won’t be accessible.

mcqs.question: If an abstract class has all the private members, then _________

options.a: a) No class will be able to implement members of abstract class
options.b: b) Only single inheritance class can implement its members
options.c: c) Only other enclosing classes will be able to implement those members
options.d: d) No class will be able to access those members but can implement.

mcqs.answer: a) No class will be able to implement members of abstract class
mcqs.explanation: The classes which inherit the abstract class, won’t be able to implement the members of abstract class. The private members will not be inherited. This will restrict the subclasses to implement those members.

mcqs.question: Which access specifier should be used so that all the parent class members can be inherited and accessed from outside the class?
mcqs.explanation: All the members must be of public access. So that the members can be inherited easily. Also, the members will be available from outside the class.

mcqs.question: Which access specifier is usually used for data members of a class?
mcqs.explanation: All the data members should be made private to ensure the highest security of data. In special cases we can use public or protected access, but it is advised to keep the data members private always.

mcqs.question: Which specifier should be used for member functions of a class?
mcqs.explanation: It is always advised that the member functions should be kept public so that those functions can be used from out of the class. This is usually done to ensure that the features provided by the class can be used at its maximum.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Private Access Specifier”.

mcqs.question: If a function has to be called only by using other member functions of the class, what should be the access specifier used for that function?
mcqs.explanation: The function should be made private. In this way, the function will be available to be called only from the class member functions. Hence the function will be secure from the outside world.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is correct for the code given below? 
class student
{  
	private: student()
	{  
	}
	public : student( int x) 
	{ 
		marks =x; 
	}
};

options.a: a) The object can never be created
options.b: b) The object can be created without parameters
options.c: c) Only the object with only 1 parameter can be created
options.d: d) Only the object with some parameters can be created

mcqs.answer: c) Only the object with only 1 parameter can be created
mcqs.explanation: For creating object without parameters, the default constructor must be defined in public access. But here, only parameterized constructor is public, hence the objects being created with only one parameter will only be allowed.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is true for the code given below? 
class A
{
	private : int marks; char name[20];
	public :
	A(int x=100)
	{ 
		marks=x;  
	}
};

options.a: a) Objects can be created with one parameter or without parameter
options.b: b) Object can be created only with one parameter
options.c: c) Object can be created with more than one parameter
options.d: d) Objects can be create only without parameter

mcqs.answer: a) Objects can be created with one parameter or without parameter
mcqs.explanation: The constructor here has a default argument constructor. Hence we can pass one parameter, but that is optional. If an object is created without parameter, the default value will be used in the constructor definition.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct to call a private member from outside the class?

options.c: c) object->memberfunction( parameteres); or object.memberfunction( parameters );

mcqs.explanation: The private member function will not be accessible from outside the class. Hence any syntax will not work to access the private members. If you have the address of the member, may be you can access those members, but that is a totally different case and concept.

mcqs.question: If private members have to be accessed directly from outside the class but the access specifier must not be changed, what should be done?

options.b: b) Friend function should be used
options.c: c) Other public members should be used

mcqs.answer: b) Friend function should be used
mcqs.explanation: For calling the function directly, we can’t use another function because that will be indirect call. Using friend function, we can access the private members directly.

mcqs.question: Which access specifier is/are most secure during inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: The private members are most secure in inheritance. The default members can still be in inherited in special cases, but the private members can’t be accessed in any case.

mcqs.question: Choose the correct option for the code given below. class A{ static int c=0; public: A(){ c++; } };

options.a: a) Constructor will make c=1 for each object created
options.b: b) Constructor will make c=0 for each object created
options.c: c) Constructor will keep number of objects created
options.d: d) Constructor will just initialize c=0 then increment by 1

mcqs.answer: c) Constructor will keep number of objects created
mcqs.explanation: The constructor is using a static member to keep the count of the number of objects created. This is done because the variable c is static and hence the value will be common for all the objects created.

mcqs.question:
Which option is false for the following code? 
class A
{
	private : int sum(int x, int y)
	{ 
		return x+y; 
	}
	public: A()
	{  
	}
	A(int x, int y)
	{ 
		cout<<sum(x,y);  
	}
};

options.a: a) Constructor can be created with zero argument
options.b: b) Constructor prints sum, if two parameters are passed with object creation
options.c: c) Constructor will give error if float values are passed
options.d: d) Constructor will take 0 as default value of parameters if not passed

mcqs.answer: d) Constructor will take 0 as default value of parameters if not passed
mcqs.explanation: Constructor is not having any default arguments hence no default value will be given to any parameters. Only integer values must be passed to the constructor if we need the sum as output, otherwise if float values are passed, type mismatch will be shown as error.

options.a: a) name variable will never be used
options.b: b) marks variable will never be used
options.c: c) constructor will never be used
options.d: d) disp() function will never be used

mcqs.answer: a) name variable will never be used
mcqs.explanation: Variable name will never be used. It is a private member. None other than class members can access name, also, neither the constructor nor the disp() function are accessing the variable name. Hence it will never be accessible.

mcqs.question: Private member functions can be overloaded.
mcqs.explanation: The private functions can also be overloaded. This can be done in usual way by having the same name of the member function and having different signature. Only thing is, they must be accessed from members of class only.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) Private member functions can’t be overloaded
options.b: b) Private member functions can be overridden
options.c: c) Private member functions can’t be overloaded with a public member
options.d: d) Private member  function can’t be overridden

mcqs.answer: d) Private member  function can’t be overridden
mcqs.explanation: The private member functions can be overloaded but they can’t be overridden. This is because, overriding means a function with same name in derived class, gets more priority when called from object of derived class. Here, the member function is private so there is no way that it can be overridden.

mcqs.question:
Which data member in following code will be used whenever an object is created? 
Class A
{ 
   int x; int y; int z;
   public : A()
   { 
      y=100; x=100*y; 
   }
};
mcqs.explanation: Whenever an object will be created, the constructor will be called. Inside constructor we are using the data members x and y. Hence these two will always be used with each object creation.

mcqs.question:
Which member can be considered most secure in the code below? 
class A()
{
	int a;
	private : int b;
	protected : int c;
	public : int d;
};
mcqs.explanation: The default variables can be inherited in some special cases but the public members can never be inherited. Hence the most secure data member in the class is b.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is correct for the code given below? 
class A
{
	private : A()
	{ 
	}
	public : A(int x)
	{  
	}
};
A a;
A b(100);

options.a: a) Program will give compile time error
options.c: c) Program will give runtime error
options.d: d) Program will give logical error

mcqs.answer: a) Program will give compile time error
mcqs.explanation: The program will be giving a compile time error as the default constructor is private in class. And, the logical errors are usually runtime so we can’t say that the program will give logical error. The program will not run.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct?

options.a: a) Private specifier must be used before public specifier
options.b: b) Private specifier must be used before protected specifier
options.c: c) Private specifier must be used first
options.d: d) Private specifier can be used anywhere in class

mcqs.answer: d) Private specifier can be used anywhere in class
mcqs.explanation: The private specifier can be used anywhere in the class as required. It is not a rule to mention the private members first and then others. It is just followed to write first for better readability.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Protected Access Specifier”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes the protected specifier?

options.a: a) Members are most secure and can’t be used outside class
options.b: b) Members are secure but can be used outside the class
options.c: c) Members are secure as private, but can be inherited
options.d: d) Members are secure like private, but can’t be inherited

mcqs.answer: c) Members are secure as private, but can be inherited
mcqs.explanation: The members which are made protected, are most secure if inheritance is not used. But, this facility is provided to keep those members private and with that, they can be inherited by other classes. This is done to make the code more flexible.

mcqs.question: If a constructor is defined in protected access, then?

options.a: a) It’s instance can be created inside the subclasses
options.b: b) It’s instance can be created anywhere in the program
options.c: c) It’s instance can be created inside the subclasses and main() function
options.d: d) It’s instance can be created inside the parent class only

mcqs.answer: a) It’s instance can be created inside the subclasses
mcqs.explanation: The instances will be allowed to be created only inside the sub classes. This is because the protected members will be inherited and hence the constructor too. This will allow the subclasses to call the constructor whenever an object is created.

mcqs.question:
For the following code, choose the correct option. 
class A
{  
	int marks;
	protected : A()
	{ 
		marks=100; 
	}
	public : A( int x)
	{ 
		marks=x;  
	}
};

options.a: a) The instances can be created only in subclasses
options.b: b) The instances can be created only in main() function
options.c: c) The instances can be created only in parent class
options.d: d) The instances can be created anywhere in the program

mcqs.answer: d) The instances can be created anywhere in the program
mcqs.explanation: The instances can be created anywhere in the program. The only restriction will be on which constructor will have to be called. The instances with zero arguments will be allowed to be created only inside the subclasses, but the instances with one argument can be created anywhere in the program.

mcqs.question: If the protected members are to be made accessible only to the nearest subclass and no further subclasses, which access specifier should be used in inheritance?

options.a: a) The sub class should inherit the parent class privately
options.b: b) The sub class should inherit the parent class as protected
options.c: c) The sub class should inherit the parent class as public
options.d: d) The sub class can use any access modifier

mcqs.answer: a) The sub class should inherit the parent class privately
mcqs.explanation: The sub class should use private inheritance. This will allow only the nearest sub classes to inherit the protected members and then those members will become private. Hence further inheritance of those members will not be possible.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output of the following code (all header files and required things are included)? 
class A
{
	int marks;
	protected : A(int x)
	{ 
		marks=x; 
	}
	public : A()
	{ 
		marks=100; 
	}
}
class B
{
	A a;
	A b=100;
};
main()
{
	A a, b=100;
	B c;
}

options.c: c) Program gives compile time error

mcqs.answer: c) Program gives compile time error
mcqs.explanation: The objects being created with assignment value are allowed, if the constructor accepts only 1 argument. But main() function will not be able to create the object here with assignment, as the constructor which accepts one argument is in protected mode in the class.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is true for the given code below? 
class A
{
	protected : int marks;
	public : 
	A()
	{ 
		marks=100; 
	}
	disp()
	{ 
		cout<<”marks=”<<marks; 
	}
};
class B: protected A
{
};
B b;
b.disp();

options.a: a) Object b can’t access disp() function
options.b: b) Object b can access disp() function inside its body
options.c: c) Object b can’t access members of class A

mcqs.answer: a) Object b can’t access disp() function
mcqs.explanation: The object of class B can’t access the members of A outside the class. This is because the class is being inherited in protected access, so all the members will become protected in subclass B.

mcqs.question: Protected members differ from default members as _______

options.a: a) Protected members can be accessed outside package using inheritance, but default can’t
options.b: b) Default members can be accessed outside package using inheritance, but protected can’t
options.c: c) Protected members are allowed for inheritance but Default members are not allowed

mcqs.answer: a) Protected members can be accessed outside package using inheritance, but default can’t
mcqs.explanation: The protected members are allowed in the same package but can also be accessed in other packages using inheritance. But the default members can never be accessible in other packages.

mcqs.question: If all the members are defined in protected specifier then? (Constructors not considered)

options.a: a) Instance of class can’t be created
options.b: b) Instance of class can be created anywhere
options.c: c) Instance of class can be created only in subclasses
options.d: d) Instance of class can be created only in main() function

mcqs.answer: b) Instance of class can be created anywhere
mcqs.explanation: The instances can be created anywhere in the program. This is because the constructors are not considered among the members defined in protected mode. Hence the default implicit constructor will be used whenever an object is created.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is correct for the code given? 
class A
{
    private: int marks;
    A()
    { 
    }
    Public : disp()
    { 
          cout<< marks; 
     }
};
class B: public A
{
}
B b;

options.a: a) Instance of B will not be created
options.b: b) Instance of B will be created
options.c: c) Program gives compile time error

mcqs.answer: a) Instance of B will not be created
mcqs.explanation: Instance of B will not be created. When you try to create an instance of B, First the constructor of parent class will be called, but the parent class constructor is private, hence it won’t be able to initialize and allocate memory for parent class members. In turn, the object of B will not be created.

mcqs.question: If protected inheritance is used then _____

options.a: a) Public members become public in subclass
options.b: b) Protected members become public in subclass
options.c: c) Protected members become protected in subclass
options.d: d) Protected and Public members become protected in subclass

mcqs.answer: d) Protected and Public members become protected in subclass
mcqs.explanation: The protected and public members of the parent class will become the protected members in subclass. This is predefined rule of inheritance. The reason behind is to maintain the level of security in subclass too.

mcqs.question: If protected members are to be accessed from outside the class then__________

options.a: a) Members must be inherited publicly in subclass
options.b: b) Members must accessed using class pointers
options.c: c) Members must be accessed as usual
options.d: d) Members must be made public

mcqs.answer: d) Members must be made public
mcqs.explanation: The members must be made public, otherwise it is not possible. In every case, the protected members will act as private members if it’s about access specifier. It will only be inherited, that too will lead to make those members protected again, in subclasses.

mcqs.question: Which among the following can use protected access specifier?

options.a: a) Members which may be used in other packages
options.b: b) Members which have to be secure and should be used by other packages/subclass
options.c: c) Members which have to be accessed from anywhere in the program
options.d: d) Members which have to be as secure as private but can be used by main() function

mcqs.answer: b) Members which have to be secure and should be used by other packages/subclass
mcqs.explanation: The members which have to be secure and might get used in other packages or subclasses can use protected access. This also allows the members to be safe from accidental modification.

mcqs.question: Protected access is same as default access that is given implicitly in java if no specifier is mentioned.
mcqs.explanation: The statement given is false. The clear difference is protected members are available in other packages also, but the default members are available within the package only.

mcqs.question: If a class have default constructor defined in private access, and one parameter constructor in protected mode, how will it be possible to create instance of object?

options.a: a) Define a constructor in public access with different signature
options.b: b) Directly create the object in the subclass
options.c: c) Directly create the object in main() function

mcqs.answer: a) Define a constructor in public access with different signature
mcqs.explanation: If a new constructor is defined in public access. That will be available to the whole program. Only restriction will be of the way to use it.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output of the program given below? 
class A
{
	Public : A(int a=0)
	{ 
		cout<<”new A”;
        }
};
A a;
A b;
A c;

options.a: a) new A new A new A
options.d: d) new A new Anew A

mcqs.explanation: The constructor has a default argument. Whenever the object is created, the constructor will be called and print the message in its definition. Since the argument is default valued, it is not mandatory to pass anything to the new object.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Public Access Specifier”.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is true for the code given below? 
class A
{
	int marks;
	public : disp()
	{ 
		cout<<marks; 
	}
}
class B: protected A
{
	char name[20];
}
A a; a.disp();
B b; b.disp();

options.a: a) Only object of class A can access disp() function
options.b: b) Only object of class B can access disp() function
options.c: c) Both instances can access disp() function
options.d: d) Accessing disp() outside class is not possible

mcqs.answer: a) Only object of class A can access disp() function
mcqs.explanation: The object of class A can access the disp() function. This is because the disp() function is public in definition of class A. But it can’t be accessed from instance of class B because the disp() function is protected in class B, since it was inherited as protected.

mcqs.question: If the members have to be accessed from anywhere in the program and other packages also, which access specifier should be used?
mcqs.explanation: The access specifier must be public so as to access the members outside the class and anywhere within the program without using inheritance. This is a rule, predefined for the public members.

mcqs.question: Which among the following have least security according to the access permissions allowed?
mcqs.explanation: The public members are available to the whole program. This makes the members most vulnerable to accidental changes, which may result in unwanted modification and hence unstable programming.

mcqs.question: Which among the following can be used for outermost class access specifier in java?
mcqs.explanation: Either default or public access specifier must be used for outermost classes. Private can be used with inner classes. This is done so that all the members can access and use the utmost class and that program execution can be done from anywhere. Inner classes can be made private for security.

mcqs.question: We can reduce the visibility of inherited methods.
mcqs.explanation: The given statement is true. This is because when we inherit the members they can either be made more secure or be at same access. For example, if a member is protected in parent class, then it can only be made protected or private in subclass and not public in any case.

mcqs.question: If members of a super class are public, then________

options.a: a) All those will be available in subclasses
options.b: b) None of those will be available in subclasses
options.c: c) Only data members will be available in subclass
options.d: d) Only member functions will be available in subclass

mcqs.answer: a) All those will be available in subclasses
mcqs.explanation: All the members will be available in subclasses. Though it is not guaranteed whether the members will be available in subsequent subclasses from the first subclass.

mcqs.question: How many public class(s) (outermost) can be there in a java program?
mcqs.explanation: There can be only one public class in a java program. The public class name must match the name of file. And there can’t be more than one class with same name in a single program in same scope. Hence it is not possible to have more than one public class in java program.

mcqs.question:
What is the output of the following code? 
package pack1;
class A
{
	public A()
	{ 
		System.out.print(“object created”); 
	}   
}
package pack2;
import pack1.*;
class B
{
	A a=new A();
}

options.b: b) Output is: object createdobject created

mcqs.explanation: The program will give compile time error. Class A is defined with default access specifier. This directly means that class A will be available within package only. Even if the constructor is public, the object will not be created.

mcqs.question: Which among the following for public specifier is false?

options.a: a) The static members can’t be public
options.b: b) The public members are available in other packages too
options.c: c) The subclasses can inherit the public members privately
options.d: d) There can be only one public class in java program

mcqs.answer: a) The static members can’t be public
mcqs.explanation: The static members are not property of any object of the class. Instead, those are treated as property of class. This allows us to have public static members too.

mcqs.question: A class has its default constructor defined as public. Class B inherits class A privately. The class ___________

options.a: a) B will not be able to have instances
options.b: b) Only A can have instances
options.c: c) Only B can have instances
options.d: d) Both classes can have instances

mcqs.answer: d) Both classes can have instances
mcqs.explanation: Class A can have instances as it has public default constructor. Class will have its own constructors defined. Hence both classes can have instances.

mcqs.question: Which specifier can be used to inherit protected members as protected in subclass but public as public in subclass?
mcqs.explanation: The specifier that can make protected member’s protected in subclass and public member’s public in subclass, is public. This is done to maintain the security level of protected members of parent class.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true for public class?

options.a: a) There can be more than one public class in a single program
options.b: b) Public class members can be used without using instance of class
options.c: c) Public class is available only within the package
options.d: d) Public classes can be accessed from any other class using instance

mcqs.answer: d) Public classes can be accessed from any other class using instance
mcqs.explanation: The public class is a usual class. There is no special rule but the members of the class can be accessed from other classes using instance of the class. This is usually useful to define main() function.

mcqs.question: If a class doesn’t have public members, then________

options.a: a) None of its members will be able to get inherited
options.b: b) None of its instance creation will be allowed
options.c: c) None of its member function can be called outside the class
options.d: d) None of its data members will be able to get initial value

mcqs.answer: c) None of its member function can be called outside the class
mcqs.explanation: According to rule of private, protected and default access specifiers, none of the members under these specifiers will be able to get invoked outside the class. We are not sure about the members of class specifically so other options doesn’t give a fixed answer.

mcqs.question: In multi-level inheritance(all public), the public members of parent/superclass will ________

options.a: a) Will continue to get inherited subsequently
options.b: b) Will not be inherited after one subclass inheritance
options.c: c) Will not be available to be called outside class
options.d: d) Will not be able to allocated with any memory space

mcqs.answer: a) Will continue to get inherited subsequently
mcqs.explanation: The public inheritance makes the public members of the base class, public in derived classes. This can be used when the same feature have to be redefined with each new class inheriting the base class.

mcqs.question: Which specifier allows to secure the public members of base class in inherited classes?
mcqs.explanation: Both the private and protected specifiers can make the public members of the base class more secure. This is useful if we stop using the parent class members and use the classes which inherited the parent class, so as to secure data better.

title: 4. OOP MCQ on Class Members & Types

links.text: Object Oriented Programming MCQ: Data Members
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Data Members”.

mcqs.question: What is the term used to indicate the variable and constants of a class?
mcqs.explanation: The variables inside a class are termed data members of the class. It is not a mandatory rule but variables are used to refer to usual variables used in functions or globally. The term is given because the values stored in those variables represent some kind of data related to class.

mcqs.question: Data members ________________ (C++)

options.a: a) Can be initialized with declaration in classes
options.b: b) Can be initialized only with help of constructors
options.c: c) Can be initialized either in declaration or by constructor

mcqs.answer: b) Can be initialized only with help of constructors
mcqs.explanation: The data members are not property of class, those are property of the instances of the class. And the memory for the data members are not reserved until a constructor is called. Hence we use constructors for their initialization after the memory is reserved.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true for data members?

options.a: a) Private data members can be initialized with declaration in class
options.b: b) Static members are initialized in constructors
options.c: c) Protected data members can be initialized in class directly
options.d: d) Static data members are defined outside class, not in constructor

mcqs.answer: d) Static data members are defined outside class, not in constructor
mcqs.explanation: Static members are not property of instances of classes. Those are shared by all the object of classes. Hence those are defined outside the constructor, so as to make them common for all the objects.

mcqs.question: What should be done for data member to be of user defined structure type?

options.a: a) The structure must have been defined before class.
options.b: b) The structure must have been defined after the class definition
options.c: c) The structure must be predefined
options.d: d) The structure type data members can’t be used

mcqs.answer: a) The structure must have been defined before class.
mcqs.explanation: The structure must have been defined prior to its use. If the structure is not defined, then the memory space will not be allocated for its members. This leads to undefined use of new data types.

mcqs.question: How many data members can a class contain?
mcqs.explanation: Any class can have as many data members as required. The only restriction that may arise is when there is not enough memory space. This gives flexibility to define a class with best properties possible.

mcqs.question: How to access data members of a class?

options.c: c) Dot or arrow as required
options.d: d) Dot, arrow or direct call

mcqs.answer: c) Dot or arrow as required
mcqs.explanation: The data members can never be called directly. Dot operator is used to access the members with help of object of class. Arrow is usually used if pointers are used.

mcqs.question: To create a pointer to a private data member of a class, outside the class, which among the following is correct?

options.a: a) Return the address of the private data member using a member function
options.b: b) Access the private member using a pointer outside class
options.c: c) Declare the member as pointer inside the class
options.d: d) Not possible to create pointer to a private member

mcqs.answer: a) Return the address of the private data member using a member function
mcqs.explanation: We can call a public member function and return the address of any private data member. Though the pointer being returned must be defined inside class itself. And the returned address can be stored in a pointer.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true for use of setter() and getter() function?

options.a: a) Considered best for manipulating data values
options.b: b) Considered the only proper way to manipulate the values
options.c: c) Considered specially for private members manipulation
options.d: d) Considered a red flag, and not recommended for large scale use

mcqs.answer: d) Considered a red flag, and not recommended for large scale use
mcqs.explanation: This concept of getter and setter functions is not acceptable if used too much. This is considered to be inappropriate in OOP perspective. Though it is commonly used, it doesn’t work according to OOP concepts at some higher level of understanding.

mcqs.question:
What is the output of following code? 
int n=10;		// global
class A()
{
	private : int n;
	public : int m;
	A()
	{ 
		n=100; m=50;
	}
void disp()
{
	cout<<”n”<<m<<n;
};
mcqs.explanation: In cout we have specified n as a string to be printed. And m is a variable so its value gets printed. And global variable will not be used since local variable have more preference.

mcqs.question: The static member functions can only use ________
mcqs.explanation: The static member functions can only access static data members. This is because the static member function can’t work with the properties that change object to object. It is mandatory that only the common properties of all the objects be used. And only static data members are common to all as those are property of class.

mcqs.question: A class can have self-referential data members.
mcqs.explanation: The data members in a class can never refer to own class type. This is not possible because the data members should have some memory allocated for its object before the self-reference is used, but class must call constructor for that. Hence not possible.

mcqs.question: What is the keyword used to make data members have same value?
mcqs.explanation: The keyword const can be used anywhere to make the variable have same value all the time. This restriction is made to use the same value whenever required. Also, this can restrict accidental changes.

mcqs.question: Which data members can be inherited but are private to a class?
mcqs.explanation: Static members inheritance also depends on the type of specifier they have. Only the protected members can be inherited but remain private to class. If static members are defined in private access, they won’t be allowed for inheritance.

mcqs.question: The arguments passed to member functions by reference are considered as data members of class.
mcqs.explanation: This is a wrong statement. As only the data defined inside class is considered as its member. But even if a variable is passed by reference it would be the same variable that is outside the class. Hence it can’t be considered class member.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is not allowed for data member declaration?
mcqs.explanation: The abstract keyword in the declaration of data members is not allowed. This is because the abstract keyword features can’t be used with the data members of the class. We can have all other syntax given, but not abstract.

links.text: Object Oriented Programming MCQ: Member Functions
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Member Functions”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes member functions?

options.a: a) Functions which are defined within the class
options.c: c) Functions in public access of a class
options.d: d) Functions which are private to class

mcqs.explanation: We can’t say that only functions that are defined inside class are member functions. There can be some inherited functions. Though they doesn’t belong to the class but are property of the objects once inheritance is used. So the nearest definition is functions belonging to a class.

mcqs.question: How many types of member functions are generally there in C++?
mcqs.explanation: There are 5 types of member functions that are generally provided in C++. Namely, simple, static, const, inline and friend member functions. Member functions are specific to classes.

mcqs.question: How can a static member function be called in the main function?

options.c: c) Using dot or arrow operator
options.d: d) Using dot, arrow or using scope resolution operator with class name

mcqs.answer: d) Using dot, arrow or using scope resolution operator with class name
mcqs.explanation: The member functions can be called using only the dot operator or the arrow operator. But the static members can be called using directly the class name followed by the scope resolution operator and static member function name. This is useful when you don’t have any object to call the member.

mcqs.question: What are inline member functions?

options.a: a) Member functions which can be called without object
options.b: b) Member functions whose definition is expanded in place of its call
options.c: c) Member functions whose definition is faster than simple function
options.d: d) Member function which is defined in single line

mcqs.answer: b) Member functions whose definition is expanded in place of its call
mcqs.explanation: The member functions whose definition is expanded at the call, and no jump to function and return happened, are termed as inline functions. This is used to make the program faster and more efficient.

mcqs.question: What happens if non static members are used in static member function?

options.d: d) Executes if that member function is not used

mcqs.explanation: There must be specific memory space allocated for the data members before the static member functions uses them. But the space is not reserved if object is not declared. Hence only if static members are not used, it leads to compile time error.

mcqs.question: Static member functions _____________

options.a: a) Contains “this” pointer for data members
options.b: b) Contains “this” pointer if used for member functions
options.d: d) Doesn’t contain “this” pointer if member functions are referred

mcqs.explanation: The static member functions doesn’t contain “this” pointer. Static member functions can’t be defined as const or volatile also. These are restrictions on static member functions.

mcqs.question: How to access members of the class inside a member function?

options.d: d) Used directly or with this pointer

mcqs.answer: d) Used directly or with this pointer
mcqs.explanation: The members of a class can be used directly inside a member function. We can use this pointer when there is a conflict between data members of class and arguments/local function variable names.

mcqs.question: For overloading “( )”, “[ ]” or “->” operators, a class __________

options.a: a) Must use static member functions
options.b: b) Must use non-static member functions
options.c: c) Must be non-static member and should not be friend of class
options.d: d) Must use static member function or a friend member function

mcqs.answer: c) Must be non-static member and should not be friend of class
mcqs.explanation: For overloading those operators for a class, the class must use non-static member function so that doesn’t remain common to all the objects, and each object can use it independently. The friend functions is also restricted so as to keep the security of data.

mcqs.question: If a virtual member function is defined ___________

options.a: a) It should not contain any body and defined by subclasses
options.b: b) It must contain body and overridden by subclasses
options.c: c) It must contain body and be overloaded
options.d: d) It must not contain any body and should not be derived

mcqs.answer: a) It should not contain any body and defined by subclasses
mcqs.explanation: The virtual functions are defined using virtual keyword. These are made in order to make all the classes to define them as the class gets inherited. Increases code understanding.

mcqs.question: Member functions of a generic class are _____________

options.c: c) To be made generic explicitly
options.d: d) Given default type as double

mcqs.explanation: When generic type is used in a class, the functions are automatically generic. This is so because the functions would use the same type as defined to make the class generic. The functions will get to know the type of data as soon as the generic class is used. It’s inbuilt feature.

mcqs.question: Member function of a class can ____________

options.a: a) Access all the members of the class
options.b: b) Access only Public members of the class
options.c: c) Access only the private members of the class

mcqs.answer: a) Access all the members of the class
mcqs.explanation: The member functions has access to all the members of the class. Whenever data members of a class, which might be private, have to be modified, we make use of these member functions. This is more secure way to manipulate data.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is proper syntax for class given below? 
class A
{ 
	int a,b;
	public : void disp();
}
mcqs.explanation: The syntax in option void A::disp(){  } is correct. We use scope resolution to represent the member function of a class and to write its definition. It is not necessary for a function to have anything in its definition.

mcqs.question: A member function can _______________ of the same class.

options.b: b) Call only private member functions
options.c: c) Call only static member functions
options.d: d) Call only const member functions

mcqs.explanation: We can call one function inside another function to access some data of class. A public member function can be used to call a private member function which directly manipulates the private data of class.

mcqs.question: Which member function doesn’t require any return type?
mcqs.explanation: All the member functions work same as normal functions with syntax. But the constructor and destructor are also considered as member functions of a class, and they never have any data type.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is not possible for member function?

options.a: a) Access protected members of parent class
options.c: c) Access public members of subclass
options.d: d) Access static members of class

mcqs.answer: c) Access public members of subclass
mcqs.explanation: A member function of a class can only have the access to the members of its own class and parent classes if inheritance used. Otherwise a member function can never access the members of a subclass. Accessing static members of a class is possible by normal and static member functions.

links.text: Object Oriented Programming MCQ: Local Class
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Local Class”.

mcqs.question: What are local classes?

options.a: a) Classes declared inside a package
options.b: b) Classes declared inside a function
options.c: c) Classes declared inside a class

mcqs.answer: b) Classes declared inside a function
mcqs.explanation: The classes declared inside a package are available to all the functions and classes, hence can’t be called local. This is somewhat similar concept that we use to denote variables of a function. The classes declared inside functions will be local to them.

mcqs.question: All member functions of a local class must be ___________

options.b: b) Defined outside the function definition
options.c: c) Defined inside the class body
options.d: d) Defined at starting of program

mcqs.answer: c) Defined inside the class body
mcqs.explanation: There is a restriction on where the member functions of the local class should be define. Those must be defined inside the class body only. This is to reduce the ambiguity and complexity of program.

mcqs.question: Can local class members access/use the general local variables (except static, abstract etc.) of the function in which it is defined?

options.a: a) Yes, it can access with arrow operator
options.b: b) No, it can’t access with dot operator
options.c: c) Yes, it can access using dot operator
options.d: d) No, it can’t access In anyway

mcqs.answer: d) No, it can’t access In anyway
mcqs.explanation: The local variables of the functions are not available to the member functions of the class. This is done to reduce the ambiguity in variables and their access rules.

mcqs.question: Which type of data can a local class access from the function in which it is defined?
mcqs.explanation: The local classes have this feature to access the static and extern variables of the function in which those are defined. This feature is available since these type of data are common to the program and is created only one time. Run time creation and destruction of these variables is not done. The only restriction that may apply is those members must be constants.

mcqs.question: Local classes can access the type names and enumerators defined by the enclosing function.
mcqs.explanation: This is a little tricky part with local classes. Though the local class can’t access the general variables of the function but can access the types that are defined inside the function. This is because the whole definition of that type would be existing inside the class.

mcqs.question: Can static variables be declared inside a local class?

options.a: a) Yes, with public access specifier
options.c: c) No, not possible in private access specifier

mcqs.explanation: No, the static variables can’t be declared inside a local class. This is because each time the function is called, all the variables get created again and are destroyed as soon as the function is returned. This would have been possible id the static variable was of function.

mcqs.question: All the member functions of local classes are __________ by default.
mcqs.explanation: All the members are defined inside the class body. And when the member functions are defined inside the class body, they are made inline by default. If the definition is too complex, those are made normal functions.

mcqs.question: The enclosing function has no special access to the members of the local class.
mcqs.explanation: This is a rule that the enclosing function doesn’t have any special access to the members of the local class. This is done to maintain the security of class members. And to adhere to the rules of OOP.

mcqs.question: Which language can use inheritance with local classes?
mcqs.explanation: Other language might support inheritance with local classes but those doesn’t provide all the proper features of inheritance. Language SAP ABAP provides a way to implement inheritance with local classes efficiently.

mcqs.question: How many local classes can be defined inside a single function?
mcqs.explanation: The local classes can be defined as required. There is no restriction on the number of local classes that can be defined inside a function. But all those classes must follow the rules and restrictions.

mcqs.question: All the data members of local class must be ___________

options.c: c) Declared and defined in constructor
options.d: d) Declared using a member function

mcqs.explanation: The data members follow the same rules as of simple classes. Hence the data members must be declared first. Then their definition must be given using the constructors.

mcqs.question: Can two different functions have local class with same name?

options.b: b) No, names must be different
options.c: c) No, scope doesn’t work here

mcqs.explanation: The local classes can have same name if they belong to different functions. The classes would be local to those specific functions and hence can have same name. This is same as that of local variables concept.

mcqs.question: What is the scope of local class?

options.d: d) One time creation and live till end of program

mcqs.explanation: The scope of a local class is limited only within the function definition. The function can use the class as usual as local variables. The class gets destroyed as soon as the function is returned.

mcqs.question: Can a function, other than the enclosing function of local class, access the class members?
mcqs.explanation: The local classes are local to the specific enclosing function. Other functions can’t access the class. Even if the pointers are used, the class must be alive when the pointer is used. But this will not happen if the enclosing function is returned.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the main advantage of using local classes?

options.c: c) Helps to add extra functionality to a function
options.d: d) Helps to add more members to a function

mcqs.answer: c) Helps to add extra functionality to a function
mcqs.explanation: The closest answer is to add more functionalities to a function or to make some specific functions to be generic. Adding more members to a function can be done directly but to add some special functionality that are encapsulated, can be done using local classes.

links.text: Object Oriented Programming MCQ: Nested Class
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Nested Class”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes a nested class?
mcqs.explanation: If a class is defined inside another class, the inner class is termed as nested class. The inner class is local to the enclosing class. Scope matters a lot here.

mcqs.question: Which feature of OOP reduces the use of nested classes?
mcqs.explanation: Using inheritance we can have the security of the class being inherited. The subclass can access the members of parent class. And have more feature than a nested class being used.

mcqs.question: How many categories are nested classes divided into?
mcqs.explanation: The nested classes are divided into two main categories. Namely, Static and non-static. The categories define how the classes can be used inside another class.

mcqs.question: Non-static nested classes have access to _____________ from enclosing class.
mcqs.explanation: The non-static nested class can access all the members of the enclosing class. All the data members and member functions can be accessed from the nested class. Even if the members are private, they can be accessed.

mcqs.question: Static nested classes doesn’t have access to _________________ from enclosing class.
mcqs.explanation: The static nested class doesn’t have access to any other members of the enclosing class. This is a rule that is made to ensure that only the data which can be common to all the object is being accessed by the static nested class.

mcqs.question: The nested class can be declared ___________________

options.d: d) Public, Protected, Private or Package private

mcqs.answer: d) Public, Protected, Private or Package private
mcqs.explanation: The nested class can be declared with any specifier, unlike the outer classes which can only be declared public or package private. This is flexibility given for the nested class being a member of enclosing class.

mcqs.question: Use of nested class ____________ encapsulation.
mcqs.explanation: The use of nested class increases encapsulation as the inner class is getting even more grouped into the enclosing class. Firstly the class encapsulate the data, having nested classes can increase the encapsulation even further.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is the correct advantage/disadvantage of nested classes?

options.a: a) Makes the code more complex
options.c: c) Makes the code efficient and readable

mcqs.answer: c) Makes the code efficient and readable
mcqs.explanation: The use of nested classes makes the code more streamed towards a single concept. This allows to group the most similar and related classes together and makes it even more efficient and readable.

mcqs.question: How to access static nested classes?
mcqs.explanation: Like any other member of the class, the static nested class uses the dot operator to be accessed. The reason behind is, the static classes can’t work with instances, hence we use enclosing class name to access static nested class.

mcqs.question: A nested class can have its own static members.
mcqs.explanation: The nested classes are associated with the object of the enclosing class. Hence have direct access to the members of that object. Hence the inner class can’t have any static members of its own. Otherwise the rule of static members would be violated using enclosing class instance.

mcqs.question: How to create object of the inner class?
mcqs.explanation: An instance of inner class can exist only within instance of outer class. To instantiate the inner class, one must instantiate the outer class first. This can be done by the correct syntax above.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output of the following code? 
public class Test
{
    public int a=0;
    class innerClass
    {
	public int a=1;
	void innermethod(int x)
	{
	    System.out.println(“value of x = ” + x);
	    System.out.println(“value of this.x = ” + this.x);
	    System.out.println(“value of Test.this.x = ” + Test.T=this.x);
	}
    }
}	
public static void main( String args[] )
{
	Test t=new Test();
	Test.innerClass im=t.new innerClass();
	im.innermethod(55);
}

options.a:
a)
  value of x = 55
  value of this.x = 0
  value of Test.this.x = 1
options.b:
b)
  value of x = 1
  value of this.x = 0
  value of Test.this.x = 55
options.c:
c)
  value of x = 55
  value of this.x = 1
  value of Test.this.x = 0
options.d:
d)
  value of x = 0
  value of this.x = 55
  value of Test.this.x = 1

mcqs.answer:
c)
  value of x = 55
  value of this.x = 1
  value of Test.this.x = 0
mcqs.explanation: The variable x denotes the parameter of the function. And this.x is the variable of the inner class. Test.this.x is the variable of the outer class. Hence we get this output.

mcqs.question: Instance of inner class can exist only _______________ enclosing class.
mcqs.explanation: The class defined inside another class is local to the enclosing class. This means that the instance of inner class will not be valid outside the enclosing class. There is no restriction for instance to be private or public always.

mcqs.question: If a declaration of a member in inner class has the same name as that in the outer class, then ________________ enclosing scope.

options.a: a) Outer declaration shadows inner declaration in
options.b: b) Inner declaration shadows outer declaration in
options.c: c) Declaration gives compile time error

mcqs.answer: b) Inner declaration shadows outer declaration in
mcqs.explanation: The inner class will have more preference for its local members than those of the enclosing members. Hence it will shadow the enclosing class members. This process is known as shadowing.

mcqs.question: A static nested class is _____________ class in behavior that is nested in another _________ class.
mcqs.explanation: Top level class encloses the other classes or have same preference as that of other top level classes. Having a class inside the top level class is indirectly having a top level class which higher degree of encapsulation.

links.text: OOPs MCQ: Passing and Returning Object with Functions
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Passing and Returning Object with Functions”.

mcqs.question: In how many ways can an object be passed to a function?
mcqs.explanation: The objects can be passed in three ways. Pass by value, pass by reference and pass by address. These are the general ways to pass the objects to a function.

mcqs.question: If an object is passed by value _____________

options.a: a) A new copy of object is created implicitly
options.b: b) The object itself is used
options.c: c) Address of the object is passed
options.d: d) A new object is created with new random values

mcqs.answer: a) A new copy of object is created implicitly
mcqs.explanation: When an object is passed by value, a new object is created implicitly. This new object uses the implicit values assignment, same as that of the object being passed.

mcqs.question: Pass by address passes the address of object _________ and pass by reference passes the address of the object _________
mcqs.explanation: Pass by address uses the explicit address passing to the function whereas pass by reference implicitly passes the address of the object.

mcqs.question: If an object is passed by reference, the changes made in the function ___________

options.a: a) Are reflected to the main object of caller function too
options.b: b) Are reflected only in local scope of the called function
options.c: c) Are reflected to the copy of the object that is made during pass
options.d: d) Are reflected to caller function object and called function object also

mcqs.answer: a) Are reflected to the main object of caller function too
mcqs.explanation: When an object is passed by reference, its address is passed implicitly. This will make changes to the main function whenever any modification is done.

mcqs.question: Constructor function is not called when an object is passed to a function, will its destructor be called when its copy is destroyed?

options.c: c) No, since no constructor was called
options.d: d) No, since same object gets used

mcqs.explanation: Even though the constructor is not called when the object is passed to a function, the copy of the object is still created, where the values of the members are same. When the object have to be destroyed, the destructor is called to free the memory and resources that the object might have reserved.

mcqs.question: When an object is returned by a function, a _______________ is automatically created to hold the return value.
mcqs.explanation: The temporary object is created. It holds the return value. The values gets assigned as required, and the temporary object gets destroyed.

mcqs.question: Is the destruction of temporary object safe (while returning object)?

options.a: a) Yes, the resources get free to use
options.b: b) Yes, other objects can use the memory space
options.c: c) No, unexpected side effects may occur
options.d: d) No, always gives rise to exceptions

mcqs.answer: c) No, unexpected side effects may occur
mcqs.explanation: The destruction of temporary variable may give rise to unexpected logical errors. Consider the destructor which may free the dynamically allocated memory. But this may abort the program if another is still trying to copy the values from that dynamic memory.

mcqs.question: How to overcome the problem arising due to destruction of temporary object?

options.b: b) Overriding functions can be used
options.c: c) Overloading parenthesis or returning object
options.d: d) Overloading assignment operator and defining copy constructor

mcqs.answer: d) Overloading assignment operator and defining copy constructor
mcqs.explanation: The problem can be solved by overloading the assignment operator to get the values that might be getting returned while the destructor free the dynamic memory. Defining copy constructor can help us to do this in even simpler way.

mcqs.question: How many objects can be returned at once?
mcqs.explanation: Like any other value, only one object can be returned at ones. The only possible way to return more than one object is to return address of an object array. But that again comes under returning object pointer.

mcqs.question:
What will be the output of the following code? 
Class A
{ 
	int i; 
	public : A(int n)
	{ 
		i=n; cout<<”inside constructor ”;
	} 
	~A()
	{
		cout<<”destroying  ”<<i;
	}
	void seti(int n)
	{
		i=n;
	}
	int geti()
	{
		return I;
	}
};
void t(A ob)
{ 
	cout<<”something ”;
}
int main()
{
	A a(1);
	t(a);
	cout<<”this is i in main ”;
	cout<<a.geti();
}

options.a: a) inside constructor something destroying 2this is i in main destroying 1
options.b: b) inside constructor something this is i in main destroying 1
options.c: c) inside constructor something destroying 2this is i in main
options.d: d) something destroying 2this is i in main destroying 1

mcqs.answer: a) inside constructor something destroying 2this is i in main destroying 1
mcqs.explanation: Although the object constructor is called only ones, the destructor will be called twice, because of destroying the copy of the object that is temporarily created. This is the concept of how the object should be passed and manipulated.

mcqs.question: It is necessary to return the object if it was passed by reference to a function.

options.a: a) Yes, since the object must be same in caller function
options.b: b) Yes, since the caller function needs to reflect the changes
options.c: c) No, the changes are made automatically
options.d: d) No, the changes are made explicitly

mcqs.answer: c) No, the changes are made automatically
mcqs.explanation: Having the address being passed to the function, the changes are automatically made to the main function. In all the cases if the address is being used, the same memory location will be updated with new values.

mcqs.question: How many objects can be passed to a function simultaneously?
mcqs.explanation: There is no limit to how many objects can be passed. This works in same way as that any other variable gets passed. Array and object can be passed at same time also.

mcqs.question: If an object is passed by address, will be constructor be called?

options.a: a) Yes, to allocate the memory
options.b: b) Yes, to initialize the members
options.d: d) No, temporary object is created

mcqs.explanation: A copy of all the values is created. If the constructor is called, there will be a compile time error or memory shortage. This happens because each time a constructor is called, it try to call itself again and that goes infinite times.

mcqs.question: Is it possible that an object of is passed to a function, and the function also have an object of same name?

options.a: a) No, Duplicate declaration is not allowed
options.b: b) No, 2 objects will be created
options.d: d) Yes, life span is different

mcqs.answer: a) No, Duplicate declaration is not allowed
