title: 9. OOPs Multiple Choice Questions on Inheritance & its Types

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Inheritance”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes the Inheritance?

options.a: a) Copying the code already written
options.b: b) Using the code already written once
options.c: c) Using already defined functions in programming language
options.d: d) Using the data and functions into derived segment

mcqs.answer: d) Using the data and functions into derived segment
mcqs.explanation: It can only be indicated by using the data and functions that we use in derived class, being provided by parent class. Copying code is nowhere similar to this concept, also using the code already written is same as copying. Using already defined functions is not inheritance as we are not adding any of our own features.

mcqs.question: How many basic types of inheritance are provided as OOP feature?
mcqs.explanation: There are basically 4 types of inheritance provided in OOP, namely, single level, multilevel, multiple and hierarchical inheritance. We can add one more type as Hybrid inheritance but that is actually the combination any types of inheritance from the 4 basic ones.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best defines single level inheritance?

options.a: a) A class inheriting a derived class
options.b: b) A class inheriting a base class
options.c: c) A class inheriting a nested class
options.d: d) A class which gets inherited by 2 classes

mcqs.answer: b) A class inheriting a base class
mcqs.explanation: A class inheriting a base class defines single level inheritance. Inheriting an already derived class makes it multilevel inheritance. And if base class is inherited by 2 other classes, it is multiple inheritance.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct for multiple inheritance?

options.a: a) class student{public:  int marks;}s;  class stream{int total;}; class topper:public student, public stream{  };
options.b: b) class student{int marks;}; class stream{ }; class topper: public student{ };
options.c: c) class student{int marks;}; class stream:public student{ };
options.d: d) class student{ }; class stream{ }; class topper{ };

mcqs.answer: a) class student{public:  int marks;}s;  class stream{int total;}; class topper:public student, public stream{  };
mcqs.explanation: Class topper is getting derived from 2 other classes and hence it is multiple inheritance. Topper inherits class stream and class student publicly and hence can use its features. If only few classes are defined, there we are not even using inheritance (as in option class student{ }; class stream{ }; class topper{ };).

mcqs.question: Which programming language doesn’t support multiple inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: Java doesn’t support multiple inheritance. But that feature can be implemented by using the interfaces concept. Multiple inheritance is not supported because of diamond problem and similar issues.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct for a hierarchical inheritance?

options.a: a) Two base classes can be used to be derived into one single class
options.b: b) Two or more classes can be derived into one class
options.c: c) One base class can be derived into other two derived classes or more
options.d: d) One base class can be derived into only 2 classes

mcqs.answer: c) One base class can be derived into other two derived classes or more
mcqs.explanation: One base class can be derived into the other two derived classes or more. If only one class gets derived by only 2 other classes, it is also hierarchical inheritance, but it is not a mandatory condition, because any number of derived classes can be there.

mcqs.question: Which is the correct syntax of inheritance?

options.a: a) class derived_classname : base_classname{ /*define class body*/ };
options.b: b) class base_classname : derived_classname{ /*define class body*/ };
options.c: c) class derived_classname : access base_classname{ /*define class body*/ };
options.d: d) class base_classname :access derived_classname{ /*define class body*/ };

mcqs.answer: c) class derived_classname : access base_classname{ /*define class body*/ };
mcqs.explanation: Firstly, keyword class should come, followed by the derived class name. Colon is must followed by access in which base class has to be derived, followed by the base class name. And finally the body of class. Semicolon after the body is also must.

mcqs.question: Which type of inheritance leads to diamond problem?
mcqs.explanation: When 2 or more classes inherit the same class using multiple inheritance and then one more class inherits those two base classes, we get a diamond like structure. Here, ambiguity arises when same function gets derived into 2 base classes and finally to 3rd level class because same name functions are being inherited.

mcqs.question: Which access type data gets derived as private member in derived class?
mcqs.explanation: It is a rule, that when a derived class inherits the base class in private access mode, all the members of base class gets derived as private members of the derived class.

mcqs.question: If a base class is inherited in protected access mode then which among the following is true?

options.a: a) Public and Protected members of base class becomes protected members of derived class
options.b: b) Only protected members become protected members of derived class
options.c: c) Private, Protected and Public all members of base, become private of derived class
options.d: d) Only private members of base, become private of derived class

mcqs.answer: a) Public and Protected members of base class becomes protected members of derived class
mcqs.explanation: As the programming language rules apply, all the public and protected members of base class becomes protected members of derived class in protected access mode. It can’t be changed because it would hinder the security of data and may add vulnerability in the program.

mcqs.question: Members which are not intended to be inherited are declared as ________________
mcqs.explanation: Private access specifier is the most secure access mode. It doesn’t allow members to be inherited. Even Private inheritance can only inherit protected and public members.

mcqs.question: While inheriting a class, if no access mode is specified, then which among the following is true? (in C++)

options.a: a) It gets inherited publicly by default
options.b: b) It gets inherited protected by default
options.c: c) It gets inherited privately by default

mcqs.answer: c) It gets inherited privately by default
mcqs.explanation: If the access mode is not specified during inheritance, the class is inherited privately by default. This is to ensure the security of data and to maintain OOP features. Hence it is not mandatory to specify the access mode if we want the class to be inherited privately.

mcqs.question: If a derived class object is created, which constructor is called first?

options.c: c) Depends on how we call the object

mcqs.explanation: First the base class constructor is invoked. When we create a derived class object, the system tries to invoke its constructor but the class is derived so first the base class must be initialized, hence in turn the base class constructor is invoked before the derived class constructor.

mcqs.question: The private members of the base class are visible in derived class but are not accessible directly.
mcqs.explanation: Consider that a variable is private in base class and the derived class uses public inheritance to inherit that class. Now if we also have a global variable of same name as that of base class private variable, neither the global variable nor the base class private variable will be accessible from derived class. This is because we can’t have 2 variables with same name in same local scope. Hence the private members are accessible but not directly.

mcqs.question: How can you make the private members inheritable?

options.a: a) By making their visibility mode as public only
options.b: b) By making their visibility mode as protected only
options.c: c) By making their visibility mode as private in derived class
options.d: d) It can be done both by making the visibility mode public or protected

mcqs.answer: d) It can be done both by making the visibility mode public or protected
mcqs.explanation: It is not mandatory that you have to make the visibility mode either public or protected. You can do either of those. That will give you permission to inherit the private members of base class.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Types of Inheritance”.

mcqs.question: How many types of inheritance are possible in C++?
mcqs.explanation: There are five types of inheritance that are possible in C++. Single level, Multilevel, multiple, hierarchical and hybrid. Here we count hybrid also because it sometimes can bring up a new form of inheritance, Like inheritance using multiple and hierarchical, which sometimes results in diamond problem.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) Java supports all types of inheritance
options.c: c) Java doesn’t support multiple inheritance

mcqs.answer: c) Java doesn’t support multiple inheritance
mcqs.explanation: Java doesn’t support multiple inheritance. This is done to avoid the diamond problem that sometimes arises with inherited functions. Though, multiple inheritance can be implemented in java using interfaces.

mcqs.question:
Which type of inheritance is illustrated by the following code? 
class student{ public: int marks; };
class topper: public student { public: char grade; };
class average{ public: int makrs_needed; };
class section: public average{ public: char name[10];  };
class overall: public average{  public: int students;  };
mcqs.explanation: It is hierarchical inheritance and single level inheritance. Since class topper is inheriting class student, it is single level inheritance. And then average is inherited by section and overall, so it is hierarchical inheritance. But both of them are separate. Hence it is not hybrid inheritance.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes multiple inheritance?

options.a: a) Two classes being parent of any other classes
options.b: b) Three classes being parent of other classes
options.c: c) More than one class being parent of other child classes
options.d: d) More than one class being parent of single child

mcqs.answer: d) More than one class being parent of single child
mcqs.explanation: If a class inherits more than one class, it is known as multiple inheritance. This should not be referred with only two or three classes being inherited. But there must be one class which inherits more than one class to be called as multiple inheritance.

mcqs.question: How many types of inheritance can be used at a time in a single program?

options.d: d) Any type, any number of times

mcqs.answer: d) Any type, any number of times
mcqs.explanation: Any type of inheritance can be used in any program. There is no rule to use only few types of inheritance. Only thing that matters is how the classes are inherited and used.

mcqs.question: Which type of inheritance results in the diamond problem?
mcqs.explanation: In diamond problem, hierarchical inheritance is used first, where two different classes inherit the same class and then in turn a 4th class inherits the two classes which had inherited the first class. Using more than one type of inheritance here, it is known as hybrid inheritance.

mcqs.question: If 6 classes uses single level inheritance with pair classes (3 pairs), which inheritance will this be called?
mcqs.explanation: Here all the pairs are using single inheritance. And no different pairs are inheriting same classes. Hence it can’t be called hybrid or multilevel inheritance. You can say the single inheritance is used 3 times in that program.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is correct for the following code? 
class A
{  
    public : class B 
    { 
        public : B(int i): data(i)
        { 
        }
        int data;
    }
};
class C: public A
{
     class D:public A::B{ };
};

options.a: a) Multi-level inheritance is used, with nested classes
options.b: b) Multiple inheritance is used, with nested classes
options.c: c) Single level inheritance is used, with enclosing classes
options.d: d) Single level inheritance is used, with both enclosing and nested classes

mcqs.answer: d) Single level inheritance is used, with both enclosing and nested classes
mcqs.explanation: Class C is inheriting Class A. Class D is inheriting class B, both are nested. Hence it is single inheritance. For multiple inheritance, class C or D should have inherited both class A and class B.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is false?

options.a: a) If one class inherits the inherited class in single level inheritance, it is multi-level inheritance
options.b: b) Hybrid inheritance always contains multiple inheritance
options.c: c) Hierarchical inheritance involves inheriting same class into more than one classes
options.d: d) Hybrid inheritance can involve any types of inheritance together

mcqs.answer: b) Hybrid inheritance always contains multiple inheritance
mcqs.explanation: It is not necessary to have multiple inheritance in hybrid type. It can have any type together. This doesn’t have to be of specific type always.

mcqs.question: If class A has two nested classes B and C. Class D has one nested class E, and have inherited class A. If E inherits B and C, then ________________

options.d: d) Multiple inheritance among nested classes, and single level for enclosing classes

mcqs.answer: d) Multiple inheritance among nested classes, and single level for enclosing classes
mcqs.explanation: This involves the same concept of inheritance, where the nested classes also follow the inheritance rules. The Enclosing classes are having single inheritance. Nested classes involves multiple.

mcqs.question: In hierarchical inheritance, all the classes involve some kind of inheritance.
mcqs.explanation: This is so because few classes might not be involved in any type of inheritance in whole program whereas other classes might be participating in more than one type of inheritance at the same time.

mcqs.question: Which type of inheritance cannot involve private inheritance?

options.d: d) All types can have private inheritance

mcqs.answer: d) All types can have private inheritance
mcqs.explanation: This is a common type of inheritance where the protected and public members of parent class become private members in child class. There is no type which doesn’t support private inheritance.

mcqs.question: How many classes can be inherited by a single class in multiple inheritance (C++)?

options.d: d) Any number of classes can be inherited

mcqs.answer: d) Any number of classes can be inherited
mcqs.explanation: Any class can inherit any number of classes. There is no limit defined for the number of classes being inherited by a single class.

mcqs.question: How many classes can be inherited by a single class in java?
mcqs.explanation: Since java doesn’t support multiple inheritance, it is not possible for a class to inherit more than 1 class in java. This is the same case in C# also.

mcqs.question: If multi-level inheritance is used, First class B inherits class A, then C inherits B and so on. Till how many classes can this go on?
mcqs.explanation: In this case, there is no limit. All the classes going on like this will inherit the members of base class, and hence the upper level inheritance won’t affect the number of classes that can go on inheriting in this pattern.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Single Level Inheritance”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following defines single level inheritance?

options.a: a) One base class derives another class
options.b: b) One derived class inherits from one base class
options.c: c) One base class inherits from one derived class
options.d: d) One derived class derives from another derived class

mcqs.answer: b) One derived class inherits from one base class
mcqs.explanation: If only one base class is used to derive only one subclass, it is known as single level inheritance. The reason of this name is that we inherit the base class to one more level and stop the inheritance any further.

mcqs.question: If class A and class B are derived from class C and class D, then ________________

options.a: a) Those are 2 pairs of single inheritance
options.d: d) Those are all independent classes

mcqs.answer: a) Those are 2 pairs of single inheritance
mcqs.explanation: Since class A is derived from class C and then class B is derived from class D, there are two pairs of classes which shows single inheritance. Those two pairs are independent of each other though.

mcqs.question: If single inheritance is used, program will contain ________________
mcqs.explanation: The program will contain at least 2 classes in the sense of base and derived classes. At least one base class and one derived class must be there. Types of inheritance remains the same though.

mcqs.question: Single level inheritance supports _____________ inheritance.
mcqs.explanation: The runtime inheritance is done when object of a class is created to call a method. At runtime the function is searched if it is in class of object. If not, it will search in its parent classes and hierarchy for that method.

mcqs.question:
Which method in the code below is single level inherited? 
class A
{
	protected int a, b;
	public: void show()
	{ 
		cout<<a<<b;
	}
};
class B: public A
{
	public: void disp()
	{ 
		cout<<a++<<b++; 
	}
};
class C: private A, public B
{
	void avg()
	{ 
		cout<<(a+b)/2; 
	}
};
mcqs.explanation: Class B is using single level inheritance. Class C is using multiple inheritance. And class A is parent of other two classes.

mcqs.question: If single level inheritance is used and an abstract class is created with some undefined functions, can its derived class also skip some definitions?

options.b: b) Yes, possible if only one undefined function
options.c: c) No, at least 2 undefined functions must be there
options.d: d) No, the derived class must implement those methods

mcqs.answer: d) No, the derived class must implement those methods
mcqs.explanation: The derived class must implement those methods. This is because the parent class is abstract and hence will have some undefined functions which has to be defined in derived classes. Since we are using single level inheritance, if derived class doesn’t implement those functions then one more class has to be there which will become multi-level inheritance.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is false for single level inheritance?

options.a: a) There can be more than 2 classes in program to implement single inheritance
options.b: b) There can be exactly 2 classes to implement single inheritance in a program
options.c: c) There can be more than 2 independent classes involved in single inheritance
options.d: d) The derived class must implement all the abstract method if single inheritance is used

mcqs.answer: c) There can be more than 2 independent classes involved in single inheritance
mcqs.explanation: If more than 2 independent classes are involved to implement the single level inheritance, it won’t be possible as there must be only one child and one parent class and none other related class.

mcqs.question: Which concept will result in derived class with more features (consider maximum 3 classes)?
mcqs.explanation: If single inheritance is used then only feature of a single class are inherited, and if multilevel inheritance is used, the 2nd class might have use private inheritance. Hence only multiple inheritance can result in derived class with more features. This is not mandatory but in a case if we consider same number of features in each class, it will result the same.

mcqs.question: Single level inheritance is safer than _____________
mcqs.explanation: Interfaces also represent a way of inheritance but is a wide word to decide which inheritance we are talking about in it, hence can’t be considered. Implementation and extensions also doesn’t match that level of specific idea. And multiple inheritance not so safe as it might result in some ambiguity.

mcqs.question: Which language doesn’t support single level inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: All the languages support single level inheritance. Since any class can inherit other classes as required, if single level inheritance was not allowed it would result in failing a lot of features of OOP.

mcqs.question:
What is the output of the following program? 
class A
{
	protected: int a,b;
	public: void disp()
	{ 
		cout<<a<<b; 
	}
};
class B:public A
{
	int x,y;
};

options.d: d) Runs but gives random values as output

mcqs.explanation: The compiler doesn’t find the main function and hence will throw an error main() missing. This program is using single level inheritance but the program is incomplete. Every program must implement main function.

mcqs.question:
What is the output of the following program? 
class A
{  
	float sal=40000;  
}  
class B extends A
{  
	int salBonus=10000;  
	public static void main(String args[])
	{  
		B p=new B();  
		System.out.println("B salary is:"+p.sal);  
		System.out.println("Bonus of B is:"+p.bonus);  
	}  
}

options.a:
a)
B salary is: 40000.0
Bonus of B is: 10000
options.b:
b)
B salary is 10000
Bonus of B is: 4000.0

mcqs.answer:
a)
B salary is: 40000.0
Bonus of B is: 10000
mcqs.explanation: The program gives output as in option a. The program have used single level inheritance and hence have access to the parent class methods and variables. This program simply prints the value from parent class and from the child class.

mcqs.question: Single level inheritance will be best for___________

options.a: a) Inheriting a class which performs all the calculations
options.b: b) Inheriting a class which can print all the calculation results
options.c: c) Inheriting a class which can perform and print all calculations
options.d: d) Inheriting all the classes for different calculations

mcqs.answer: b) Inheriting a class which can print all the calculation results
mcqs.explanation: Inheriting a class which can perform the most common task will be more efficient. If class which can perform all the calculations is inherited then there won’t be any problem to print the result too. But if a class which can do the most common task for all the other tasks, it will make real use of inheritance.

mcqs.question: Which constructor will be called first from the classes involved in single inheritance from object of derived class?

options.c: c) Both class constructors at a time

mcqs.explanation: The base class constructor will be called first from the object of derived class constructor. When the derived class members are to be initialized and allocated memory, the base class members should also be confirmed with the memory allocation.

mcqs.question: If base class contains 2 nested classes, will it be possible to implement single level inheritance?

options.b: b) Yes, only if derived class also have nested classes
options.c: c) No, it will use more than 2 classes which is wrong

mcqs.explanation: The nested classes are also members of a class. They behave as a used defined data type with some methods implementation. So the inheritance will be as usual with the nested classes being member of base class and of derived class if not private.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Multilevel Inheritance”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best defines multilevel inheritance?

options.a: a) A class derived from another derived class
options.b: b) Classes being derived from other derived classes
options.d: d) Class which have more than one parent

mcqs.answer: b) Classes being derived from other derived classes
mcqs.explanation: Only if the class is being derived from other derived class, it can be called as multilevel inheritance. If a class is derived from another class, it is single level inheritance. There must be more than one level of inheritance.

mcqs.question: If there are 5 classes, E is derived from D, D from C, C from B and B from A. Which class constructor will be called first if the object of E or D is created?
mcqs.explanation: A is parent of all other classes indirectly. Since A is parent of B and B is parent of C and so on till E. Class A constructor will be called first always.

mcqs.question: If there are 3 classes. Class C is derived from class B and B is derived from A, Which class destructor will be called at last if object of C is destroyed.
mcqs.explanation: The destructors are called in the reverse order of the constructors being called. Hence in multilevel inheritance, the constructors are created from parent to child, which leads to destruction from child to parent. Hence class A destructor will be called at last.

mcqs.question: Which Class is having highest degree of abstraction in multilevel inheritance of 5 levels?
mcqs.explanation: The class with highest degree of abstraction will be the class at the 1st level. You can look at a simple example like, a CAR is more abstract than SPORTS CAR class. The level of abstraction decrease with each level as more details comes out.

mcqs.question: If all the classes use private inheritance in multilevel inheritance then ______________

options.a: a) It will not be called multilevel inheritance
options.b: b) Each class can access only non-private members of its parent
options.c: c) Each subsequent class can access all members of previous level parent classes
options.d: d) None of the members will be available to any other class

mcqs.answer: b) Each class can access only non-private members of its parent
mcqs.explanation: The classes will be able to access only the non-private members of its parent class. The classes are using private inheritance, hence all the members of the parent class become private in the derived class. In turn those won’t be allowed for further inheritance or direct access outside the class.

mcqs.question: Multilevel inheritance allows _________________ in the program.

options.b: b) At least 7 levels of inheritance
options.c: c) At most 16 levels of inheritance
options.d: d) As many levels of inheritance as required

mcqs.answer: d) As many levels of inheritance as required
mcqs.explanation: The multilevel inheritance allows any number of levels of inheritance. This is the maximum flexibility feature to make the members available to all the new classes and to add their own functionalities. The code reusability is used too.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum number of levels for a implementing multilevel inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: There must be at least 3 levels of inheritance. Otherwise if less, it will be single level inheritance or would have got no inheritance implemented. There must be a derived class from which another class is derived.

mcqs.question: In multilevel inheritance one class inherits _______________

options.d: d) As many classes as required

mcqs.explanation: The classes inherit only from one class. This continues as each class inherits only one class. There should not be any class that inherits from two or more classes or which have more than one subclass.

mcqs.question: All the classes must have all the members declared private to implement multilevel inheritance.
mcqs.explanation: There is no mandatory rule to make the members private for multilevel inheritance. Moreover, if all the classes have only the private members then there won’t be any member to get inherited. Hence the working will be of no use.

mcqs.question: Can abstract classes be used in multilevel inheritance?

options.b: b) Yes, only one abstract class
options.c: c) No, abstract class doesn’t have constructors

mcqs.explanation: The abstract classes can always be used in multilevel inheritance. The only condition that may arise is that all the undefined functions must be defined in subclasses. There must not be any undefined function.

mcqs.question: How many abstract classes can be used in multilevel inheritance?

options.c: c) At least one less than number of levels

mcqs.answer: c) At least one less than number of levels
mcqs.explanation: At least one class must implement all the undefined functions. Hence there must be at least one class which is not abstract. That is at least one less than number of levels.

mcqs.question: If all the classes used parameterized constructors and no default constructor then ___________

options.a: a) The object of lower level classes can’t be created
options.b: b) Object of lower level classes must call parent class constructors explicitly
options.c: c) Object of lower level classes must define all the default constructors
options.d: d) Only object of first class can be created, which is first parent

mcqs.answer: b) Object of lower level classes must call parent class constructors explicitly
mcqs.explanation: Each class constructor must be called before creating the object of any subclass. Hence it will be mandatory to call the constructors of parent classes explicitly with parameters. This will make all the previous class member be initialized and then the class in use will be able to create the object.

mcqs.question: In multilevel inheritance, which is the most significant feature of OOP used?
mcqs.explanation: The classes using multilevel inheritance will use the code in all the subsequent subclasses if available. Hence the most significant feature among the options given is code reusability. This feature is generally intended to use the data values and reuse the redundant functions.

mcqs.question:
Does following code show multiple inheritance? 
 
class A
{
	int a;
};
class B
{
	int b;
};
class C:public A, public B
{
	int c;
};
class D:public C
{
	int d;
};

options.a: a) Yes, class C and class D
options.b: b) Yes, All together it’s multilevel
options.d: d) No, multiple inheritance is used with class A, B and C

mcqs.answer: d) No, multiple inheritance is used with class A, B and C
mcqs.explanation: Since multiple inheritance is used to derive class C and then class D is derived from class C. This is not multilevel inheritance. The classes should derive from single class. This is actually hybrid inheritance.

mcqs.question: Is it compulsory for all the classes in multilevel inheritance to have constructors defined explicitly if only last derived class object is created?

options.b: b) Yes, to initialize the members
options.d: d) No, Constructor must not be defined

mcqs.explanation: It’s not mandatory to define the constructors explicitly. Default constructor will always be provided by the compiler itself if none another constructor is defined in those classes. If explicit default constructor is defined it will be used.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Multiple Inheritance”.

mcqs.question: Multiple inheritance is ____________________

options.a: a) When a class is derived from another class
options.b: b) When a class is derived from two or more classes
options.c: c) When a class is derived from other two derived classes
options.d: d) When a class is derived from exactly one class

mcqs.answer: b) When a class is derived from two or more classes
mcqs.explanation: The multiple inheritance is used when a class is being derived using two base classes or more. This way a single class can have features of more than one classes inherited into a single unit. This lets us combine two class members into a single class.

mcqs.question: Which problem arises due to multiple inheritance, if hierarchical inheritance is used previously for its base classes?
mcqs.explanation: The diamond problem arises when multiple inheritance is used. This problem arises because the same name member functions get derived into a single class. Which in turn creates ambiguity in calling those methods.

mcqs.question: How many classes should a program contain to implement the multiple inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: For the implementation of multiple inheritance, there must be at least 3 classes in a program. At least 2 base classes and one class to inherit those two classes. If lesser, it becomes single level inheritance.

mcqs.question: Which programming language restricts the use of multiple inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: Java doesn’t allow use of multiple inheritance with classes. But this can be done by using the interfaces. This is more secure and unambiguous way to implement multiple inheritance.

mcqs.question: Is it possible to have all the abstract classes as base classes of a derived class from those?

options.b: b) Yes, only if derived class implements all the methods
options.c: c) No, because abstract classes doesn’t have constructors

mcqs.answer: b) Yes, only if derived class implements all the methods
mcqs.explanation: The condition for abstract class applies same here too. All the undefined functions must be defined. Hence all the base classes can be abstract but derived class must implement all those undefined functions.

mcqs.question: If class A inherits class B and class C as “class A: public class B, public class C {// class body ;}; ”, which class constructor will be called first?
mcqs.explanation: The constructors of parent class will be called first. In that, the constructor of the classes will be called in the same sequence as that mentioned in class definition inheritance. Since class B is mentioned first for inheritance, its constructor will be called first.

mcqs.question: Why does diamond problem arise due to multiple inheritance?

options.a: a) Methods with same name creates ambiguity and conflict
options.b: b) Methods inherited from the superclass may conflict
options.c: c) Derived class gets overloaded with more than two class methods
options.d: d) Derived class can’t distinguish the owner class of any derived method

mcqs.answer: a) Methods with same name creates ambiguity and conflict
mcqs.explanation: All the derived classes can distinguish the base class members, but if a method is being inherited to the base classes from another class which again gets inherited into same class (diamond shape), that may create conflict in using the function from two available.

mcqs.question: How many base classes can a derived class have which is implementing multiple inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: The classes can derive from as many classes as required since the multiple inheritance feature is made to combine or group together the functions that are from different classes. This make the derived class stronger in terms of its flexibility.

mcqs.question: How to overcome diamond problem?

options.c: c) Using virtual keyword with same name function

mcqs.answer: c) Using virtual keyword with same name function
mcqs.explanation: To overcome the ambiguity and conflict we can use keyword virtual. This will help us to differentiate the functions with same name that came to last derived class in diamond problem.

mcqs.question: When multiple inheritance is used, which class object should be used in order to access all the available members of parent and derived class?

options.d: d) Derive a class from derived class

mcqs.explanation: The derived class object can access all of its own members. It can also access the available members of the parent classes, because the members are derived into the derived class.

mcqs.question: If all the members of all the base classes are private then _____________

options.a: a) There won’t be any use of multiple inheritance
options.b: b) It will make those members public
options.c: c) Derived class can still access them in multiple inheritance

mcqs.answer: a) There won’t be any use of multiple inheritance
mcqs.explanation: The derived class will not be able to access any members of the base classes. Since private member’s are not inheritable. It leads to no use of multiple inheritance.

mcqs.question: Is it compulsory to have constructor for all the classes involved in multiple inheritance?

options.b: b) Yes, only if no abstract class is involved
options.c: c) No, only classes being used should have a constructor
options.d: d) No, they must not contain constructors

mcqs.answer: b) Yes, only if no abstract class is involved
mcqs.explanation: The constructors must be defined in every class. If class is abstract, it won’t have any constructor but other classes must have constructor. Either implicit or explicit.

mcqs.question: If a class contains 2 nested class and is being inherited by another class, will there be any multiple inheritance?

options.a: a) No, only single level inheritance is used
options.b: b) No, only multilevel inheritance is used
options.c: c) Yes, because 3 classes are involved
options.d: d) Yes, because more than 1 classes are being derived

mcqs.answer: a) No, only single level inheritance is used
mcqs.explanation: When a class having nested classes is being derived into another class. It indirectly means a simple class is being inherited to another class. This is single level inheritance.

mcqs.question: Which members can’t be accessed in derived class in multiple inheritance?

options.d: d) All the members of base

mcqs.explanation: The private member’s are available for only the class containing those members. Derived classes will have access to protected and public members only.

mcqs.question: Can the derived class be made abstract if multiple inheritance is used?

options.a: a) No, because other classes must be abstract too
options.b: b) Yes, if all the functions are implemented
options.c: c) Yes, if all the methods are predefined
options.d: d) No, since constructors won’t be there

mcqs.answer: d) No, since constructors won’t be there
mcqs.explanation: The derived class must not be abstract. This is because the abstract classes doesn’t have constructor and hence we won’t be having the capability to have instances. This will restrict the use of multiple inheritance.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Hierarchical Inheritance”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is best to define hierarchical inheritance?

options.a: a) More than one classes being derived from one class
options.b: b) More than 2 classes being derived from single base class
options.c: c) At most 2 classes being derived from single base class
options.d: d) At most 1 class derived from another class

mcqs.answer: a) More than one classes being derived from one class
mcqs.explanation: When two or more classes get derived from a single base class, it is known as hierarchical inheritance. This gives us freedom to use same code with different scopes and flexibility into different classes.

mcqs.question: Do members of base class gets divided among all of its child classes?

options.b: b) Yes, depending on  type of inheritance
options.c: c) No, it’s doesn’t get divided
options.d: d) No, it may or may not get divided

mcqs.answer: c) No, it’s doesn’t get divided
mcqs.explanation: The class members doesn’t get divided among the child classes. All the members get derived to each of the subclasses as whole. The only restriction is from the access specifiers used.

mcqs.question: Each class can inherit the base class ________________

options.b: b) Independently with private inheritance only
options.c: c) With same type of inheritance
options.d: d) With each class using different inheritance only

mcqs.explanation: The classes can inherit the base class using any type of inheritance. There is no mandatory condition to use same private,public or protected inheritance only.

mcqs.question: How many classes must be there to implement hierarchical inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: At least 3 classes must be there. Two derived classes and one base class. This lets us implement two classes that have common characteristics from base class.

mcqs.question: Base class  _______________

options.d: d) If made abstract, compile time error

mcqs.explanation: The base class may or may not be declared abstract. It depends on the need of program. If it is made abstract, it can contain undefined functions too. In turn, those functions will have to be implemented by each of the derived classes.

mcqs.question: Which access specifiers should be used so that all the derived classes restrict further inheritance of base class members?

options.d: d) Any inheritance type can be used

mcqs.explanation: All the derived classes must use private inheritance. This will make the members of base class private in derived classes. Hence none of the members of base class will be available for further inheritance.

mcqs.question:
Which class uses hierarchical inheritance in following code? 
class A
{
	int a;
};
class B:class A
{
	int b;
};
class C:class A,class B
{
	int c;
};
class D:class A
{
	int d;
};
mcqs.explanation: Class A is base class and B and D are derived classes. If class C is considered, it shows hybrid inheritance, involving single level and multiple inheritance.

mcqs.question:
Which among the following is correct for following code? 
abstract class A
{
	public Int a;
	public void disp();
};
class B:public A
{
	public: void dis()
	{ 
		court<<a; 
	}
};
class C:private A
{
	public void incr()
	{ 
		a++; 
	}
}
void main()
{
	B b.disp();
}

options.c: c) Program runs and o/p is 0
options.d: d) Program runs and o/p is garbage value

mcqs.explanation: The derived class D have not implemented the undefined function. Here the main concept involves hierarchical inheritance with abstract base class.

mcqs.question: How many classes can be derived from the base class using hierarchical inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: The number of classes that can be derived from a base class doesn’t have any restriction and hence will be able to derive as many classes as required. This feature gives more flexibility and code reusability.

mcqs.question: If one class have derived the base class privately then another class can’t derive the base class publically.
mcqs.explanation: The classes are independent and can access the base class and inherit it in whichever way it is required. The classes can use the base base class members privately or publically maintaining the security of data and methods.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) Hierarchical inheritance is subset of multiple inheritances
options.b: b) Hierarchical inheritance is strongest inheritance type
options.c: c) Hierarchical inheritance uses only 2 classes for implementation
options.d: d) Hierarchical inheritance allows inheritance of common features to more than one class

mcqs.answer: d) Hierarchical inheritance allows inheritance of common features to more than one class
mcqs.explanation: Hierarchical inheritance is used to make all the inherited classes have some common features obtained from a single base class. This allows all the classes to maintain a group or to be classified under one class.

mcqs.question: Hierarchical inheritance can be a subset of _________________
mcqs.explanation: When we use hybrid inheritance, it can contain any type of inheritance or combination or more than two types. Hence it may contain Hierarchical inheritance too, hence it can be subset of hybrid inheritance.

mcqs.question: Which type of inheritance is most suitable for inheriting Same syllabus into different colleges with different streams?
mcqs.explanation: When hierarchical inheritance is used, the common syllabus can be adopted into different college classes where the same syllabus is applicable. For changing the syllabus only the details of base class will have to changed.

mcqs.question: Which class constructor is called first when an object of derived class is created?

options.c: c) Firstly created derived class constructor
options.d: d) Last created derived class constructor

mcqs.explanation: The base class must be initialised first hence the constructor of base class is called first. This makes everything ready for the new object being created.

mcqs.question: All the derived classes can access only a few members of base class that other derived classes can’t access at same time, in hierarchical inheritance.
mcqs.explanation: The derived classes have full access to all the non private member’s of base class. Every derived class have equal access, none of the class can have special access to specific members of base class in general cases.

links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Hybrid Inheritance”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best defines the hybrid inheritance?

options.a: a) Combination of two or more inheritance types
options.b: b) Combination of same type of inheritance
options.c: c) Inheritance of more than 7 classes
options.d: d) Inheritance involving all the types of inheritance

mcqs.answer: a) Combination of two or more inheritance types
mcqs.explanation: When more than one type of inheritance are used together, it results in new type of inheritance which is in general known as hybrid inheritance. This may of may not have better capabilities.

mcqs.question: How many types of inheritance should be used for hybrid?
mcqs.explanation: There must be combination of at least 2 types of inheritance. The inheritance should be of different type.

mcqs.question: If single inheritance is used with class A and B. A is base class. Then class C, D and E where C is base class and D is derived from C, then E is derived from D. Class C is made to inherit from class B. Which is the resultant type?
mcqs.explanation: The statement represents multilevel inheritance. It is not hybrid since looking at complete idea, one can’t differentiate whether two type of inheritance are used. Hence it is multilevel inheritance.

mcqs.question: Diamond problem includes ____________________ hybrid inheritance.
mcqs.explanation: The diamond problem arises when more than one classes are derived from one class and then those classes are used to derive single clas. Resulting in ambiguity of same functions from each class.

mcqs.question: If __________________ inheritance is done continuously, it is similar to tree structure.
mcqs.explanation: Hierarchical inheritance is deriving more than one classes from a base class, it it is done continuously and subsequently, it results forming a tree like structure of classes being linked.

mcqs.question: Which amongst the following is true for hybrid inheritance?

options.a: a) Constructor calls are in reverse
options.b: b) Constructor calls are priority based
options.c: c) Constructor of only derived class is called

mcqs.explanation: The constructors will be called in usual way. First the parent class Constructor and then the derived class Constructors. This is done to initialise all the members properly.

mcqs.question: Which type of inheritance must be used so that the resultant is hybrid?
mcqs.explanation: The use of any specific type is not necessary. Though the final structure should not be the same, it should represent more than one type of inheritance if class diagram is drawn.

mcqs.question: The private member’s are made public to all the classes in inheritance.
mcqs.explanation: The private member’s scope can’t be changed and those can never be accessed in other classes. Only the class containing private member’s can access its own members.

mcqs.question: If hierarchical inheritance requires to inherit more than one class to single class, which syntax is correct? (A, B, C are class names)

options.a: a) hierarchical class A: public B, public C
options.b: b) multiple class A: public B, public C
options.c: c) many class A: public B, public C
options.d: d) class A: public B, public C

mcqs.answer: d) class A: public B, public C
mcqs.explanation: The syntax is as same as declaration of other classes. There is no specific keyword defined for using hybrid inheritance in programming. Only thing is to specify the class name separated by commas.

mcqs.question: What is the maximum number of classes allowed in hybrid inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: The classes in any type of inheritance can inherit as many classes as required. The only condition that may arise is memory management. The classes can inherit most of the features from more than one class.

mcqs.question: What is the minimum number of classes to be there in a program implementing hybrid inheritance?
mcqs.explanation: The answer is no limit. There is no condition defined for limit of classes that has to be used in hybrid. Though you must have at least 4 classes so that one set of multiple or hierarchical inheritance is there and one more class to use single level inheritance.

mcqs.question: If object of lowest level class is created (last derived class) ________________  of its parent class constructors are called.
mcqs.explanation: When derived class object is created, all of its successor parent classes constructors are called. Constructor of all the connected classes is not created. Since the parent members have to be initialised, but other derived classes are not needed.

mcqs.question: If hybrid inheritance is used, it mostly shows _______________ feature of OOP.
mcqs.explanation: The code is reusable in most of the classes and the data becomes more linked to other classes. Other features are also exhibited, but the code reusability is used the most. Code readability becomes relatively less. Flexibility increases but it depends on how the hybrid inheritance is used.

mcqs.question: The sequence of destructors being called while using hybrid inheritance is ____________

options.a: a) Reverse of constructors being called
options.b: b) Reverse of classes being made
options.c: c) Reverse of objects being created
options.d: d) Reverse of code calling objects

mcqs.answer: a) Reverse of constructors being called
mcqs.explanation: The destructors are always called in reverse order of constructors being called always. The type of inheritance doesn’t matter. The only important concept is the sequence of classes being inherited.

mcqs.question: Overloading operators are possible only by using hybrid inheritance.
mcqs.explanation: The overloading concept is not related to the types of inheritance being used. Overloading operators can be done without using inheritance. You don’t even have to use more than one class for operator overloading.

title: 12. OOP MCQ on Member Functions & its Types

links.text: Object Oriented Programming MCQ: Virtual Functions
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Virtual Functions”.

mcqs.question: Virtual function is ______ class function which expected to be redefined in ______ class, so that when reference is made to derived class object using pointer then we can call virtual function to execute ________ class definition version.
mcqs.explanation: The functions which may give rise to ambiguity due to inheritance, can be declared virtual. So that whenever derived class object is referred using pointer or reference to the base class methods, we can still call the derived class methods using virtual function. Hence this differentiates those methods from each other.

mcqs.question: What does a virtual function ensure for an object, among the following?

options.a: a) Correct method is called, regardless of the class defining it
options.b: b) Correct method is called, regardless of the object being called
options.c: c) Correct method is called, regardless of the type of reference used for function call
options.d: d) Correct method is called, regardless of the type of function being called by objects

mcqs.answer: c) Correct method is called, regardless of the type of reference used for function call
mcqs.explanation: It is property of the virtual function and one of their main use. Its use ensure that the correct method is called even though it is been called from different pointer or references. This also decreases chance of mistakes in program.

mcqs.question: Virtual functions are mainly used to achieve _____________
mcqs.explanation: It is used to achieve runtime polymorphism. The functions which are inherited and overridden, so at runtime the correct function is executed. The correct function call is made from the intended class.

mcqs.question: Which keyword is used to declare virtual functions?
mcqs.explanation: The virtual keyword is used to declare virtual functions. Anonymous keyword is used with classes and have a different meaning. The virtual functions are used to call the intended function of the derived class.

mcqs.question: Where the virtual function should be defined?

options.c: c) Base class and derived class

mcqs.explanation: The virtual function should be declared in base class. So that when the derived class inherits from the base class, the functions can be differentiated from the one in base class and another in derived class.

mcqs.question: The resolving of virtual functions is done at ______________
mcqs.explanation: The resolving of virtual functions that are to be called is done at run time. The base class and the derived classes may contain different definitions and different variables, so all these things are resolved at run time and decided which function is to be called.

mcqs.question: In which access specifier should a virtual function be defined?
mcqs.explanation: The virtual functions must be defined in public section of a class. This is to ensure that the virtual function is available everywhere in the program. Also to avoid any error while resolving the method.

mcqs.question: Virtual functions can never be made _______________
mcqs.explanation: The virtual function must not be static. Those functions are the property of individual objects and not of a class as a whole. The functions should not be made common for all the objects of that class.

mcqs.question: Virtual functions can’t be made friend function of other classes.
mcqs.explanation: The friend functions can access the private members also. This may hinder the security of class members. This is why the functions should not be made friend functions of other class.

mcqs.question: Which is a must condition for virtual function to achieve runtime polymorphism?

options.a: a) Virtual function must be accessed with direct name
options.b: b) Virtual functions must be accessed using base class object
options.c: c) Virtual function must be accessed using pointer or reference
options.d: d) Virtual function must be accessed using derived class object only

mcqs.answer: c) Virtual function must be accessed using pointer or reference
mcqs.explanation: The virtual functions must be called using pointer or reference. This is mandatory so that the intended function gets executed while resolving the method at runtime. The must not be any ambiguity between the method of parent class and derived class.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true for virtual functions?

options.a: a) Prototype must be different in base and derived class
options.b: b) Prototype must be same in base class and derived class
options.c: c) Prototype must be given only in base class
options.d: d) Prototype must have different signature in base and derived class

mcqs.answer: b) Prototype must be same in base class and derived class
mcqs.explanation: The prototype must be the same. Because the function is to be overridden in the derived class. If the function prototype is different in derived class then it will not override the base class function and hence virtual function concept won’t work here.

mcqs.question: The virtual functions must be declared and defined in _____________ class and overridden in ___________ class.
mcqs.explanation: The virtual functions must be declared and defined in base class. The functions can be redefined in derived class. If redefined in derived class then it overrides the base class function definition.

mcqs.question: It is __________ to redefine the virtual function in derived class.
mcqs.explanation: It is not necessary to redefine the virtual function in the derived class. If not defined, the base class function definition is used but if defined, the intended definition is used according to need. It is not about good coding practice as it should be redefined only if needed.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) A class may have virtual destructor but not virtual constructor
options.b: b) A class may have virtual constructor but not virtual destructor
options.c: c) A class may have virtual constructor and virtual constructor
options.d: d) A class may have either virtual destructor or virtual constructor

mcqs.answer: a) A class may have virtual destructor but not virtual constructor
mcqs.explanation: Any class can contain virtual destructor. But is not possible to define a virtual constructor. The reason behind is that the destructors can be overridden but constructors should not be.

mcqs.question: If virtual function of base class is redefined in derived class then ________________

options.a: a) It must be declared virtual in derived class also
options.b: b) It may or may not be declared virtual in derived class
options.c: c) It can must not be declared virtual in derived class
options.d: d) It must be declared normally in derived class

mcqs.answer: b) It may or may not be declared virtual in derived class
mcqs.explanation: The virtual functions may or may not be declared virtual in derived class. This is because if the overriding function defined in derived class is not declared virtual explicitly, the compiler makes it virtual implicitly.

links.text: Object Oriented Programming MCQ: Abstract Function
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on ” Abstract Function”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best defines the abstract methods?

options.a: a) Functions declared and defined in base class
options.b: b) Functions only declared in base class
options.c: c) Function which may or may not be defined in base class
options.d: d) Function which must be declared in derived class

mcqs.answer: b) Functions only declared in base class
mcqs.explanation: The abstract functions must only be declared in base class. Their definitions are provided by the derived classes. It is a mandatory condition.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) The abstract functions must be only declared in derived classes
options.b: b) The abstract functions must not be defined in derived classes
options.c: c) The abstract functions must be defined in base and derived class
options.d: d) The abstract functions must be defined either in base or derived class

mcqs.answer: a) The abstract functions must be only declared in derived classes
mcqs.explanation: The abstract functions can’t be defined in base class. They are to be defined in derived classes. It is a rule for abstract functions.

mcqs.question: How are abstract functions different from the abstract functions?

options.a: a) Abstract must not be defined in base class whereas virtual function can be defined
options.b: b) Either of those must be defined in base class

mcqs.answer: a) Abstract must not be defined in base class whereas virtual function can be defined
mcqs.explanation: The abstract functions are only declared in base class. Derived classes have to implement those functions in order to inherit that base class. The functions are always defined in derived classes only.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct?

options.a: a) Abstract functions should not be defined in all the derived classes
options.b: b) Abstract functions should be defined only in one derived class
options.c: c) Abstract functions must be defined in base class
options.d: d) Abstract functions must be defined in all the derived classes

mcqs.answer: d) Abstract functions must be defined in all the derived classes
mcqs.explanation: The abstract function are only declared in base classes and then has to be defined in all the derived classes. This allows all the derived classes to define own definition of any function whose declaration in base class might be common to all the other derived classes.

mcqs.question: It is ____________________ to define the abstract functions.

options.a: a) Mandatory for all the classes in program
options.b: b) Necessary for all the base classes
options.c: c) Necessary for all the derived classes
options.d: d) Not mandatory for all the derived classes

mcqs.answer: c) Necessary for all the derived classes
mcqs.explanation: The derived classes must define the abstract function of base class in their own body. This is a necessary condition. Because the abstract functions doesn’t contain any definition in base class and hence becomes mandatory for the derived class to define them. All the functions in a program must have some definition.

mcqs.question: The abstract function definitions in derived classes is enforced at _________
mcqs.explanation: When the program is compiled, these definitions are checked if properly defined. This compiler also ensure that the function is being defined by all the derived classes. Hence we get a compile time error if not done.

mcqs.question: What is this feature of enforcing definitions of abstract function at compile time called?

options.d: d) Static or dynamic according to need

mcqs.explanation: The feature is known as Dynamic polymorphism. Because the definitions are resolved at runtime. Even though the definitions are checked at compile time, they are resolved at runtime only.

mcqs.question: What is the syntax for using abstract method?
mcqs.explanation: The syntax must firstly contain the access modifier. Then the keyword abstract is written to mention clearly to the compiler that it is an abstract method. Then prototype of the function with return type, function name and parameters.

mcqs.question: If a function declared as abstract in base class doesn’t have to be defined in derived class then ______

options.a: a) Derived class must define the function anyhow
options.b: b) Derived class should be made abstract class
options.c: c) Derived class should not derive from that base class
options.d: d) Derived class should not use that function

mcqs.answer: b) Derived class should be made abstract class
mcqs.explanation: If the function that is not to be defined in derived class but is declared as abstract in base class then the derived class must be made an abstract class. This will make the concept mandatory that the derived class must have one subclass to define that method.

mcqs.question: Static methods can’t be made abstract in java.
mcqs.explanation: The abstract functions can’t be made static in a program. If those are made static then the function will be a property of class rather than each object. In turn ever object or derived class must use the common definition given in the base class. But abstract functions can’t be defined in the base class. Hence not possible.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) Abstract methods can be static
options.b: b) Abstract methods can be defined in derived class
options.c: c) Abstract methods must not be static
options.d: d) Abstract methods can be made static in derived class

mcqs.answer: c) Abstract methods must not be static
mcqs.explanation: The abstract methods can never be made static. Even if it is in derived class, it can’t be made static. If this happens, then all the subsequent sub classes will have a common definition of abstract function which is not desirable.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is correct for abstract methods?

options.a: a) It must have different prototype in the derived class
options.b: b) It must have same prototype in both base and derived class
options.c: c) It must have different signature in derived class
options.d: d) It must have same return type only

mcqs.answer: b) It must have same prototype in both base and derived class
mcqs.explanation: The prototype must be the same. This is to override the function declared as abstract in base class. Or else it will not be possible to override the abstract function of base class and hence we get a compile time error.

mcqs.question: If a class have all the abstract methods the class will be known as ___________
mcqs.explanation: The classes containing all the abstract methods are known as abstract classes. And the abstract classes can never have any normal function with definition. Hence known as abstract class.

mcqs.question: The abstract methods can never be ___________ in a base class.
mcqs.explanation: The base class must not contain the abstract methods. The methods have to be derived and defined in derived class. But if it is made private it can’t be inherited. Hence we can’t declare it as a private member.

mcqs.question: The abstract method definition can be made ___________ in derived class.
mcqs.explanation: The derived class implements the definition of the abstract methods of base class. Those can be made private in derived class if security is needed. There won’t be any problem in declaring it as private.

links.text: Object Oriented Programming MCQ: Types of Member Functions
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Types of Member Functions”.

mcqs.question: How many types of member functions are possible in general?
mcqs.explanation: There are basically 5 types of member functions possible. The types include simple, static, const, inline, and friend member functions. Any of these types can be used in a program as per requirements.

mcqs.question: Simple member functions are ______________________

options.a: a) Ones defined simply without any type
options.b: b) Ones defined with keyword simple
options.c: c) Ones that are implicitly provided
options.d: d) Ones which are defined in all the classes

mcqs.answer: a) Ones defined simply without any type
mcqs.explanation: When there is no type defined for any function and just a simple syntax is used with the return type, function name and parameter list then those are known as simple member functions. This is a general definition of simple members.

mcqs.question: What are static member functions?

options.a: a) Functions which use only static data member but can’t be accessed directly
options.b: b) Functions which uses static and other data members
options.c: c) Functions which can be accessed outside the class with the data members
options.d: d) Functions using only static data and can be accessed directly in main() function

mcqs.answer: d) Functions using only static data and can be accessed directly in main() function
mcqs.explanation: The static member functions can be accessed directly in the main function. There is no restriction on direct use. We can call them with use of objects also. But the restriction is that the static member functions can only use the static data members of the class.

mcqs.question: How can static member function can be accessed directly in main() function?
mcqs.explanation: The static member functions can be accessed directly in the main() function. The only restriction is that those must use only static data members of the class. These functions are property of class rather than each object.

mcqs.question: Correct syntax to access the static member functions from the main() function is ______________
mcqs.explanation: The syntax in option b must be followed in order to call the static functions directly from the main() function. That is a predefined syntax. Scope resolution helps to spot the correct function in the correct class.

mcqs.question: What are const member functions?

options.a: a) Functions in which none of the data members can be changed in a program
options.b: b) Functions in which only static members can be changed
options.c: c) Functions which treat all the data members as constant and doesn’t allow changes
options.d: d) Functions which can change only the static members

mcqs.answer: c) Functions which treat all the data members as constant and doesn’t allow changes
mcqs.explanation: The const member functions are intended to keep the value of all the data members of a class same and doesn’t allow any changes on them. The data members are treated as constant data and any modification inside the const function is restricted.

mcqs.question: Which among the following best describes the inline member functions?

options.a: a) Functions defined inside the class only
options.b: b) Functions with keyword inline only
options.c: c) Functions defined outside the class
options.d: d) Functions defined inside the class or with the keyword inline

mcqs.answer: d) Functions defined inside the class or with the keyword inline
mcqs.explanation: The functions which are defined with the keyword inline or are defined inside the class are treated to be inline functions. Definitions inside the class are implicitly made inline if none of the complex statements are used in the definition.

mcqs.question: What are friend member functions (C++)?

options.a: a) Member function which can access all the members of a class
options.b: b) Member function which can modify any data of a class
options.c: c) Member function which doesn’t have access to private members
options.d: d) Non-member functions which have access to all the members (including private) of a class

mcqs.answer: d) Non-member functions which have access to all the members (including private) of a class
mcqs.explanation: A non-member function of a class which can access even the private data of a class is a friend function. It is an exception on access to private members outside the class. It is sometimes considered as a member functions since it has all the access that a member function in general have.

mcqs.question: What is the syntax of a const member function?
mcqs.explanation: The general syntax to be followed in order to declare a const function in a class is as in option a. The syntax may vary in different programming languages.

mcqs.question: Which keyword is used to make a nonmember function as friend function of a class?
mcqs.explanation: The keyword friend is provided in programming languages to use it whenever a functions is to be made friend of one class or other. The keyword indicates that the function is capable of new functionalities like accessing private members.

mcqs.question: Member functions _____________________

options.a: a) Must be defined inside class body
options.b: b) Can be defined inside class body or outside
options.c: c) Must be defined outside the class body
options.d: d) Can be defined in another class

mcqs.answer: c) Must be defined outside the class body
mcqs.explanation: The functions definitions can be given inside or outside the body of class. If defined inside, general syntax is used. If defined outside then the class name followed by scope resolution operator and then function name must be given for the definition.

mcqs.question: All type of member functions can’t be used inside a single class.
mcqs.explanation: There is no restriction on the use of type of member functions inside a single class. Any type any number of times can be defined inside a class. The member functions can be used as required.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is true?

options.a: a) Member functions can never be private
options.b: b) Member functions can never be protected
options.c: c) Member functions can never be public
options.d: d) Member functions can be defined in any access specifier

mcqs.answer: d) Member functions can be defined in any access specifier
mcqs.explanation: The member functions can be defined inside any specifier. There is no restriction. The programmer can apply restrictions on its use by specifying the access specifier with the functions.

mcqs.question: Which keyword is used to define the static member functions?
mcqs.explanation: The static keyword is used to declare any static member function in a class. The static members become common to each object of the class being created. They share the same values.

mcqs.question: Which keyword is used to define the inline member function?
mcqs.explanation: The inline keyword is used to defined the inline member functions in a class. The functions are implicitly made inline if defined inside the class body, but only if they doesn’t have any complex statement inside. All functions defined outside the class body must be mentioned with an explicit inline keyword.

links.text: Object Oriented Programming MCQ: Member Operator Function
links.context: This set of Object Oriented Programming (OOPs) using C++ Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on “Member Operator Function”.

mcqs.question: Which among the following are valid ways of overloading the operators?

options.c: c) Either member functions or friend functions can be used

mcqs.answer: c) Either member functions or friend functions can be used
mcqs.explanation: The operators can be overloaded by using the member function or even the friend functions can be used. This is because both of these can access all the data members of a class.

mcqs.question: Which among the following is mandatory condition for operators overloading?

options.a: a) Overloaded operator must be member function of the left operand
options.b: b) Overloaded operator must be member function of the right operand
options.c: c) Overloaded operator must be member function of either left or right operand
options.d: d) Overloaded operator must not be dependent on the operands

mcqs.answer: a) Overloaded operator must be member function of the left operand
mcqs.explanation: The operator to be overloaded must be made the member function of the operand on left side of expressions to be used. This allows the compiler to identify whether the overloading has to be used or not. This rule also reduces the ambiguity in code.

mcqs.question: When the operator to be overloaded becomes the left operand member then ______________

options.a: a) The right operand acts as implicit object represented by *this
options.b: b) The left operand acts as implicit object represented by *this
options.c: c) Either right or left operand acts as implicit object represented by *this
options.d: d) *this pointer is not applicable in that member function

mcqs.answer: b) The left operand acts as implicit object represented by *this
mcqs.explanation: The left operand becomes the object that is referred by *this pointer in the member function that will be called while using operator overloading. This is done to point to a specific object on which the overloading will be applied.

mcqs.question: If the left operand is pointed by *this pointer, what happens to other operands?

options.a: a) Other operands are passed as function return type
options.b: b) Other operands are passed to compiler implicitly
options.c: c) Other operands must be passed using another member function
options.d: d) Other operands are passed as function arguments

mcqs.answer: d) Other operands are passed as function arguments
mcqs.explanation: The operands that are used during overloading expect the left operand, can be passed as function arguments. Those are then referred in function definition with the names specified in the argument list.

mcqs.question: If a friend overloaded operator have to be changed to member overloaded operator, which operator should be used with the class name?
mcqs.explanation: The scope resolution operator can be used followed by the class name. Then the operator keyword with the operator symbol that should be overloaded. This is done to use member function instead of friend function.

mcqs.question: What is the syntax to overload an operator?
mcqs.explanation: The class name is followed by the scope resolution operator. This is done to specify the class to which the function should belong to. Then the keyword operator should be used in order to indicate the operator that is to be overloaded. Then come the parameters list to specify other operands.

mcqs.question: Why the left parameter is removed from parameter list?

options.a: a) Because it is of no use
options.b: b) Because it is never used in definitions
options.c: c) Because it becomes parameter pointed by *this
options.d: d) Because it can’t be referred by *this pointer

mcqs.answer: c) Because it becomes parameter pointed by *this
mcqs.explanation: The left object is removed from being passed as a parameter, because it is implicitly passed. It is passed implicitly because it is considered the object with respect to which the overloading function is being called.

mcqs.question: Which object’s members can be called directly while overloading operator function is used (In function definition)?
mcqs.explanation: This is because the left operand is passed implicitly. It is pointed by *this. This in turn means we can use the direct member names of the object because those are again converted to a syntax containing *this pointer implicitly.

mcqs.question: If left operand member is specified directly in the function definition, which is the correct implicit conversion of that syntax?
mcqs.explanation: Since the left operands are passed implicitly, those object members can be accessed directly in the function definition. The compiler converts the syntax into the syntax that can be processed. The implicitly converted syntax contains *this pointer followed by the objectName that is left operand in the expression.

mcqs.question: When the friend operator overloading is converted into member operator overloading _______________

options.a: a) Two parameters of friend function remains same parameters in member operator overloading
options.b: b) Two parameters of friend function becomes only one parameter of member function
options.c: c) Two parameters of friend function are removed while using member function
options.d: d) Two parameters of friend function are made 4 in member operator overloading

mcqs.answer: b) Two parameters of friend function becomes only one parameter of member function
mcqs.explanation: The friend function would accept two arguments if some binary operator is overloaded. When we try to convert that definition to member operator overloading then it becomes only one parameter. The reason behind is that the left operand is passed implicitly while using the member functions.

mcqs.question: Where in the parameter list is the implicit *this is added?

options.d: d) Not added to parameter list

mcqs.explanation: The left operand is passed implicitly by the compiler to the member function. But this is done, when the compiler adds the calling object as *this to the parameter list. It is always added as the left most parameter, i.e. the first parameter of the function.

mcqs.question: Which operator among the following can be overloading using only member function?
mcqs.explanation: Only the assignment operator among the options given must be overloaded using the member functions. The assignment operator can’t be overloaded using friend function. This is a restriction in the programming languages to make the programs more resistant towards errors.
